title: System Development Engineer, ADC AIML
description:
Are you passionate about building resilient, scalable systems that power critical services? As a System Development Engineer at Amazon, you will design and deliver technology solutions that improve operational health, reduce complexity, and enable teams to move faster with higher quality. You will own the engineering and operational excellence of your team's systems, identifying risks and eliminating them with permanent fixes. Your work will directly improve the customer experience by making systems more reliable, maintainable, and cost-effective. If you are a curious, self-starter who thrives on solving difficult problems and coaching others to do the same, this role offers the opportunity to make meaningful impact across teams.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph. The position further requires the candidate to opt into a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver technology solutions that solve difficult business problems, ensuring they are thoroughly tested, pragmatic, efficient, and cost-effective.
- Improve your team's operational health by participating in design reviews, operational readiness reviews, and post-incident analyses to identify risks to resilience, then deliver projects that mitigate those risks.
- Deeply diagnose problems across hardware, software, and operating environments, resolving contributing causes of performance, reliability, and availability issues with permanent solutions.
- Automate repetitive tasks, develop monitoring metrics, and identify points of failure to continuously improve system resiliency and reduce operational burden.
- Write clear, accurate documentation and contribute to code reviews, providing meaningful feedback to peers while coaching others on identifying and eliminating risk.

A day in the life
You will start your day reviewing system health dashboards and addressing any operational alerts that surfaced overnight. From there, you might dive into designing an automation solution that eliminates a recurring manual process, participate in a post-incident review to uncover root causes, or pair with teammates on a code review. You will collaborate with partner teams to align on system dependencies and share operational best practices.

About the team
Our team is focused on building and maintaining systems that are reliable, scalable, and easy to operate. We invest in engineering excellence and automation so that we can deliver products and services to customers with less effort and better quality. We value collaboration, inclusive problem-solving, and continuous improvement. If you want to grow your technical leadership skills while making a tangible difference in how systems perform at scale, we would love to have you join us.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

title: Licensed Alcohol & Drug Counselor
description:
Sign-On Bonus Available!
$1,000 for ADC-Ts
$2,000 for LADCs

Summary
Under indirect supervision, this individual provides a range of substance use disorder counseling services to individuals, groups, and/or families as appropriate to the specific expectations of the position. This individual typically works under indirect guidance of a clinical professional within the environment of a paraprofessional staff, and new employees as required.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
• Provide substance use disorder counseling services as defined in the 12 Core Functions as stated in Minnesota Statutes Chapter 148F:
o CORE FUNCTIONS – screening; intake; orientation; assessment; treatment planning; counseling (group, individual and family); case management; crisis intervention; client education; referral; reports; recordkeeping; and consultation with other professionals regarding client treatment and services.
• Follow and support CADT’s philosophy, policies, procedures, and job responsibilities.
• Develop and maintain appropriate professional relationships with referral sources and community agencies.
• Diagnose substance use disorders.
• Meet with families to identify needs for services and to make appropriate referrals.
• Participate in meetings – team staffing, staff meetings and consultations.
• Maintain records according to CADT policy and procedures, and licensing regulations.
• Work as an active and effective member of the treatment team.
• Demonstrate interest and willingness to increase skills and knowledge regarding substance use disorders and participate in activities that advance the field of substance use disorder treatment.
• Maintain a professional demeanor within the agency and the community.
• May participate in training sessions and workshops to enhance treatment skills.
• Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
• Must be a Licensed Alcohol and Drug Counselor. (LADC)
o Or have a temporary permit. (ADC-T)
o Or be exempt from licensure under Minnesota Statutes Chapter 148F.
• Must document competence in screening for and working with mental health problems through a 12-hour education program and experience.
• Must be CPR and First Aid certified or obtain it before direct patient contact.
• Must pass background studies issued by the Minnesota Department of Human Services.

Individual exempt from MN Statues chapter 148F must complete the following:
• Bachelor’s degree with a major in Social Work, Nursing, Sociology, Human Services, or Psychology; or must be a registered nurse;
• A minimum of 120 hours of classroom instruction in which each of the core functions as listed in 148F are covered; and
• Must complete 440 hours of supervised experience as an alcohol and drug counselor, either as a student or staff member.
Individuals with a temporary permit from the Board of Behavioral Health and Therapy may provide chemical dependency treatment service if they meet either of the requirements below:
• The individual with a temporary permit must be supervised by a licensed alcohol and drug counselor assigned by the license holder. The supervising licensed alcohol and drug counselor must document the amount and type of supervision provided at least on weekly basis. The supervision must relate to clinical practice.
• The individual with a temporary permit must be supervised by a Clinical Supervisor approved by the Board of Behavioral Health and Therapy. The supervision must be documented and meet the requirements of section 148F.04, subdivision 4.

Hours: TBD

Compensation and Benefits:
We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package to support your health, well-being, and professional growth.

  • Hourly Pay: $24-$32 per hour.
  • Health Insurance: Comprehensive coverage with 80% employer contribution toward the lowest-cost Gold Plans.
  • Dental & Vision Insurance: Coverage options available for both dental and vision care.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO): Generous paid time off to support work-life balance.
  • Paid Holidays: 10 paid holidays each year.
  • Development Time: Dedicated paid time for professional development and continuing education.
  • Retirement Plans:
    • 401(k) & Roth IRA: 4% employer base contribution, plus an additional 4% employer match.
  • Life Insurance: Employer-paid life insurance for peace of mind.
  • Disability Insurance:
    • Short-Term Disability: 100% employer coverage for short-term disabilities.
    • Long-Term Disability: 100% employer coverage for long-term disabilities.
  • Accidental & Critical Illness Insurance: Additional coverage to help in the event of unexpected accidents or illnesses.
  • Health Savings Account (HSA): Available for eligible plans to help you save for medical expenses with tax advantages.
  • On-the-Job Training: Comprehensive training to support your growth and success in your role.
  • Paid Continuing Education (CEU) Training: Paid time and funding for continuing education to maintain your licensure and skills.
  • Tuition Assistance: Financial support for higher education through our tuition assistance programs.
  • Tuition Forgiveness: Eligibility for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) and Minnesota State Programs.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Confidential counseling and support services for personal and family matters.
  • Family & Medical Leave: Time off for medical or family reasons in accordance with state and federal laws.
  • Additional Leave Benefits: Paid leave for Bereavement, Jury Duty, and Military Leave.

Degree of Authority

Perform duties under the direct supervision of the Treatment Director, Clinical Supervisor, Assistant Medical Director, and the policies and procedures that govern activity at the Center for Alcohol & Drug Treatment.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described herein are representative of those that must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.

Physical Demands

The physical demands and work environment described herein are representative of those that must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this job.
Limited physical effort is required. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk, listen, stand, walk, use hands to handle, grab, and feel, to taste and smell. The employee is occasionally required to sit, reach with hands and arms, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Specific vision requirements include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. This individual must be able to read, write and comprehend.

Work Environment

This individual’s work environment is normally performed in a typical office setting. The work environment involves some exposure to hazards or physical risks, which require following basic safety precautions. This individual may rarely be exposed to blood or body fluids. The noise level is generally quiet to moderate.
This position is designated as in-person. The Center reserves the right to modify the work arrangement based on operational needs, patient requirements, and performance considerations.

VISION: The Center for Alcohol & Drug Treatment’s vision is a community in which people’s potential and quality of life are not limited by addiction and its consequences.

MISSION: The Center for Alcohol & Drug Treatment’s mission is to improve personal, family and community health through addiction prevention, treatment and recovery services.

Visit our Website: cadt.org
Find us on LinkedIn: www.linkedin.com/company/cadt-mn/
Follow us on Instagram: instagram.com/cadt_duluth/

The Center for Alcohol & Drug Treatment will consider all applicants regardless of their race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, marital status, familial status, or status with regard to public assistance, or membership or activity in a local human rights commission.

title: Help Desk II
description:
Position Overview

The Help Desk II Technician serves as an escalation point for complex support tickets, providing advanced troubleshooting and technical leadership within the help desk team. This role involves managing tickets end-to-end, implementing technical solutions, and mentoring junior technicians. You will work across diverse client environments to ensure operational stability and high service quality.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a Tier 2 escalation for Help Desk I technicians, resolving advanced hardware, software, and network issues.
  • Support and manage Microsoft 365, Intune, and Active Directory environments, including GPOs and security configurations.
  • Troubleshoot Windows 10/11 OS issues, user profile corruption, printer/network connectivity, and MFA-related problems.
  • Manage endpoint security and patching through tools like SentinelOne, ThreatLocker, and N-able.
  • Document technical processes and knowledge base articles for internal use.
  • Collaborate with infrastructure and project teams to assist with deployments and server upgrades.
  • Perform proactive system monitoring and maintenance to ensure uptime and performance.
  • Communicate technical solutions clearly to clients and team members.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Strong technical proficiency across Windows environments, networking fundamentals, and Microsoft cloud services.
  • Experience with ticket triage, prioritization, and root cause analysis in an MSP setting.
  • Familiarity with common COTS tools (SentinelOne, ThreatLocker, DUO, N-able, etc.).
  • Strong communication, customer service, and mentoring abilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple client environments and competing priorities effectively.
  • Security-first mindset with focus on compliance and best practices.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or related discipline preferred.
  • 3+ years of IT support experience, ideally in a Managed Service Provider or professional services environment.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft 365, Intune, and MFA and DNS.
  • Need some exposure to Firewalls.
  • Certifications such as CompTIA Network+, Microsoft 365 Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator, or equivalent preferred.

Work Environment:

  • Fast-paced, collaborative MSP culture with opportunities to expand into project work or system administration.
  • Exposure to enterprise-grade tools and clients across multiple industries.

title: Product Owner Lead (Payments)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Product Owner Lead (Payments) based in Switzerland.

Lead the product direction for a portfolio of payment products, including payment aggregation, integrations, and related services.
Shape a shared product vision and align priorities with broader business objectives and customer needs.
Guide and mentor Product Owners while ensuring strong collaboration across product, technical, and operational teams.
Own the delivery of the core payment aggregator service and help ensure reliable execution across the wider payments domain.
Work directly with B2B customers to understand requirements, support integrations, and participate in technical discussions.
Drive improvements to product processes, documentation, analytics, and standards within a fast-moving international environment.
Help build scalable payment solutions while balancing customer experience, technical complexity, operational needs, and business priorities.

Accountabilities

  • Define and maintain a shared vision for payment products, including payment aggregation, payment integrations, and supporting services, ensuring alignment with business objectives.
  • Collaborate with Product Owners to align and prioritize the product roadmap across the payments domain.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop Product Owners, supporting them with prioritization, stakeholder management, and product decision-making.
  • Act as Product Owner for the team responsible for developing the core payment aggregator service.
  • Oversee high-quality and timely delivery across payment product areas, coordinating priorities and resolving delivery challenges.
  • Work directly with B2B customers to gather and validate requirements, coordinate integrations, participate in technical discussions, and monitor SLA execution.
  • Coordinate dependencies and collaboration between product, engineering, technical, and operational teams, including resolving complex issues and conflicts.
  • Establish and improve shared product processes, standards, and ways of working across the payments function.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date product documentation in collaboration with technical writers, including API documentation and integration guides.

    • Requirements:

    • 5+ years of experience working as a Product Owner, including at least 1 year in a Lead role.
    • Strong hands-on expertise in the payments domain, including PSPs, payment gateways, payment orchestration, antifraud solutions, reconciliation, and transaction matching.
    • Intermediate-level English or higher, with confidence in both written and spoken communication.
    • Experience managing the full product lifecycle, from discovery and validation through delivery and continuous improvement.
    • Proven experience with B2B products, including customer communication, requirements gathering, and integration management.
    • Practical understanding of Product Discovery, Product Delivery, and Agile/Scrum methodologies.
    • Experience with API-first products, including the ability to read API specifications and work with logs and transaction data.
    • Working knowledge of web technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SQL, together with a basic understanding of UX/UI principles.
    • Strong stakeholder management, communication, prioritization, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
    • Experience in gambling or betting is considered an advantage but is not essential.
    • Additional value comes from experience integrating with third-party casino platforms, working with crypto payments or alternative payment methods, or understanding PCI DSS, AML/KYC, and payment regulations.
    • Familiarity with payment analytics and metrics such as conversion rate, approval rate, and provider-level success rates is a plus.
    • Knowledge of product testing processes and quality assurance practices is also beneficial.

      • Benefits:

      • Fully remote work, with the option to work from hubs in Kyiv or Warsaw.
      • 20 paid working days off, public holidays, and paid sick leave to support work-life balance.
      • Medical insurance with access to leading clinics.
      • Coverage for psychological support through the Pleso platform.
      • Monthly Benefit Cafe allowance that can be used for hobbies, sports, and other personal interests.
      • Team events, workshops, masterclasses, team-building activities, and corporate events.

      • Clear career development opportunities supported by performance reviews and mentoring programs.
      • Opportunities to work on technology products from the ground up while using automation to reduce routine work.

title: Software Engineer (Platform Engineering)
description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Software Engineer is an independent contributor who delivers features end-to-end, contributes to team-level improvements, and operates effectively across multiple parts of the tech stack. The position shapes technical solutions, refines requirements with Product Managers, and improves code quality and code maintainability leveraging software engineering principles and practices.

The Platform Engineering specialization focuses on building and maintaining shared tooling, pipelines, platform capabilities, and infrastructure-as-code resources that improve developer productivity and system reliability across MBTA technology teams. This specialization enables product and application teams to adopt best-practice standards for quality, security, observability, deployment automation, cost efficiency, and operational resilience. Platform Engineers develop infrastructure-as-code models to use AWS-based resources and create other tools, patterns and automation that strengthens MBTA’s overall software engineering ecosystem.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Perform a wide variety of software engineering tasks primarily in the relevant languages.
  • Deliver and maintain well-architected features from design through implementation.
  • Demonstrate strong fundamental coding and debugging skills by writing reliable, maintainable code while demonstrating a strong understanding of possible tradeoffs to meet deadlines by effectively articulating impacts and proposing solutions.
  • Contribute to on-call rotations and address routine incidents.
  • Follow engineering standards, including code reviews, documentation, and testing. Participate and offer constructive feedback to improve.
  • Improve maintainability and reduce complexity through refactoring.
  • Investigate defects and lead feasibility assessments to identify improvements.
  • Protect data security, compliance, and privacy across all work activities by following secure coding practices.
  • Participate in team rituals (stand-ups, planning, retros).
  • Work collaboratively with UX and PMs to refine requirements for difficult problems and reduce unnecessary scope.
  • Participate in on-call rotation of technology systems and services.
  • Perform all other duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location specific functions.

Supervision
  • No direct reports.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.
  • Two (2) years of relevant professional experience in software engineering.
  • Experience independently delivering features end-to-end to solve problems.
  • Experience applying software engineering principles and practices to quickly and creatively achieve team or project goals.
  • Experience with monitoring, on-call, incident response, and reliability engineering.
  • Strong debugging and investigative skills.
  • Experience with software testing best practices and CI/CD.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into technology.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in at least one or more programming languages.
  • As part of the selection process, candidates will be asked to complete and pass job-related technical assessments, which may include a software design diagramming exercise and/or a timed coding exercise.
  • Ability to participate in on-call rotation of technology systems and services.
Substitutions
  • A high school diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
  • An associate’s degree from an accredited institution and an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
  • A master’s degree in a related subject substitutes for two (2) years of general experience.
  • A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one (1) year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

  • More than four (4) years of relevant professional experience in software engineering.
  • Solid understanding of APIs, data flows, and failure modes.
  • Experience with Elixir.
  • Experience with AWS.
  • Experience in public sector, transportation agency, and/or civic technology team.
  • Experience with Terraform / OpenTofu / Infrastructure as Code tools.
  • Experience in agile software development practices.
  • Knowledge of transit data standards (such as GTFS, GTFS-RT, TODS, TIDES).
  • Experience building or maintaining platform-level tools that support development productivity, CI/CD workflows, or automated testing.
  • Experience with AWS services used in platform or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience using Infrastructure-as-Code tools (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi) to manage cloud resources.
  • Experience operating or building pipeline, orchestration, or observability tooling.
  • Experience developing automation that improves reliability, deployment frequency, or operational consistency across multiple engineering teams.
  • Experience implementing secure coding, cost-management, or resiliency patterns at the platform layer.

Job Conditions:

  • Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
  • Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
  • Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
  • Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
  • Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
  • Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
  • Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
  • Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
  • Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.

Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.

title: Administrative Program Specialist A
description:
About this Job

The Mission of ELMHS is to provide mental health evaluation, treatment, habilitation, and consultation for adults. Programs include inpatient interventions, jail-based evaluations, supervised group home and residential programs, forensic evaluation, care, custody, and aftercare; intermediate and long-term psychiatric are in coordination with the total system of care in Louisiana.

ELMHS is looking for a motivated, detail-oriented, and positive individual to join our team as an Administrative Program Specialist A! The selected candidate will coordinate Fiscal Department operations by providing administrative support, maintaining records and timekeeping, facilitating communication and policy implementation, assisting with budget preparation, and supporting compliance with state and federal requirements.

An ideal candidate will possess the following competencies:
Accepting Direction: The ability to be open and willing to follow guidance or instructions.
Demonstrating Accountability: The ability to take ownership of actions, behaviors, performance, decisions, and outcomes.
Following Policies and Procedures: The ability to follow, reinforce, adapt, or develop policies and procedures to maintain compliance with federal and state legal requirements, State Civil Service rules, and organizational policies.
Managing Resources: The ability to manage financial, physical, and contractual resources to ensure compliance and maximize business value.
Acting Decisively: The ability to make timely, confident decisions using sound reason.
Acting with Ethics and Integrity: The ability to make choices that reflect ethical standards, integrity, and honesty, regardless of circumstances or personal benefit.
Adapting to Change: The ability to demonstrate flexibility in thoughts, behaviors, and actions in response to evolving circumstances or unexpected change.
Championing Continuous Improvement: The ability to promote and implement ongoing enhancements in processes, products, services, or organizational culture.

Minimum Qualifications

Three years of experience in administrative services; OR

Six years of full-time work experience in any field; OR

A bachelor's degree.

EXPERIENCE SUBSTITUTION:
Every 30 semester hours earned from an accredited college or university will be credited as one year of experience towards the six years of full-time work experience in any field. The maximum substitution allowed is 120 semester hours which substitutes for a maximum of four years of experience in any field.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

In this role, you will:

  • Plan, coordinate, and carry out all functions related to the purchasing of goods, services, equipment, repairs and renovations for Eastern LA Mental Health System ensuring that all purchases are made according to the rules and regulations of the state of Louisiana procurement code.

  • Be responsible for the management of electronic requisition systems for procurement card, purchase orders, and inventory transactions.

  • Provide assistance and back up support for purchases made through LaGov and by Procurement Card.

  • Be responsible for preparing and processing yearly service and maintenance contract renewals, contract amendments and new contracts.

  • Be responsible for receiving, reviewing, obtaining contract monitor's approval and processing for payment monthly invoices.

  • Be responsible for preparing the monthly invoice payment rep01t, preparing the monthly facility project report, the monthly department QA data, the monthly departmental dashboard data, the Quarterly LaPas Performance Indicator data, the outstanding p-card transaction report used for projection purposes, and other reports as needed by Fiscal Director.

  • Be responsible for assisting and providing backup to the Office of Risk Management Liaison by organizing casualty and property insurance, vehicle insurance and general insurance claims.

  • Assists in securing coverage through the Division of Administration's Office of Risk Management (ORM).

  • Assists in preparing and submitting to ORM all vehicle accident and property loss claims (both personal and agency).

Park Nicollet is hiring for a Laboratory Assistant III position to help support the Eden Prairie, Chanhassen, and Wayzata Clinics.


POSITION SUMMARY STATEMENT:

The Lab Assistant will provide a wide range of laboratory services including specimen collection, client service and reception desk duties, ordering/ scheduling/ billing functions, laboratory testing, phlebotomy, dispatching, specimen processing, centrifuging, delivery of specimens to appropriate lab/ department and assuring proper efficiency and workflow management. Position will also serve as a resource for questions from hospital and clinic staff regarding specimen handling and processing.

    • Strong customer service skills, ability to work independently, good problem-solving skills.

    • Demonstrates knowledge of age-related growth and development principles necessary to provide appropriate service and assure safety of patients.

    • Demonstrates strong organizational skills with the ability to meet time sensitive customer requests and changes on short notice.



PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Education, Experience or Equivalent Combination:

    • 1-2 years of previous laboratory or healthcare experience preferred.

    • One year hospital experience preferred.

    4. Interacts with the Supervisors and Team Leads daily to report issues and concerns involving Lab Assistants and customers.

    5. Attends and/or completes all assigned PNHS mandatory training and Laboratory specific competency testing as scheduled.

    6. Participates in completion of performance appraisals using the automated electronic system to provide input for self, peers, staff, and leaders.

    2. Performs established quality control, preventative maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting programs to ensure reliable, operational instruments and accuracy and validity of results. Maintains appropriate documentation. Documents appropriate corrective action as directed.

    4. Calls and documents critical results as appropriate per policy.

title: Budget Management Analyst
description:
Nature and Variety of Work



Come join our team!


Prince George’s County Government provides a dynamic and inclusive workplace where employees can thrive, learn, and grow across its 30 diverse agencies, all dedicated to serving the County's residents with essential resources and services. Nestled just minutes away from Washington, DC, Prince George's County combines urban vibrancy with serene surroundings, offering an ideal setting to live, work, and enjoy life.


The Prince George’s County Department of Family Services is currently seeking qualified applicants to fill a Budget Management Analyst (Budget Management Analyst 1A), grade A18/21, in the Management Services Division.


About the Position

This is entry-level trainee professional level staff work, either assisting with conducting detailed analyses and providing recommendations concerning County Government or other County Agency’s operating and capital budgets, performing moderately complex special issue and project management assignments, and/or performing program evaluation and management analyses assignments. Personal contacts for employees in this class are primarily with other employees and supervisors in the Office of Management and Budget, and Budget Management Liaisons within assigned Departments/Agencies. The purpose of these contacts is to advise, persuade, often negotiate, and otherwise present analyses and recommendations about issues which have significant impact on operating and capital budget formulation and decision making, and other issues which have either political, legal, fiscal, social, environmental, tax rate and/or service delivery implications. Incumbents work under the general direction and guidance of a Budget Management Analyst IV or higher, who makes assignments by defining objectives, priorities and deadlines.

About the Agency

The Department of Family Services improves the quality of life and overall well-being of the communities by providing information, assistance and referrals, as well as promoting and developing high quality, innovative programs that educate, empower, respect choice and preserve dignity. The department is responsible for providing assistance to some of the County’s most vulnerable citizens – children, families, victims of domestic violence, people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, veterans, and seniors. The department is comprised of three divisions that serve the aging and disabled, victims of domestic violence, as well as children, youth and families in need of support and resources.

Examples of Work


  • Develops budgetary and program data for assigned Departmental program areas.
  • Leads supporting and program staff in the development of program budgets and the preparation of internal reports as requested.
  • Prepares and submits program expenditure reports.
  • Prepares fiscal analysis of program expenditures.
  • Ensures that all program expenditures incurred are in compliance with County, State and Federal regulations for assigned program areas.
  • Reviews internal expenditure requests to ensure that funding is adequate.
  • Processes expenditure requests in a timely fashion.
  • Reviews County reports and documents to determine if expenditures incurred are appropriate.
  • Prepares journal entries or other corrective action to correct any unauthorized expenditures.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Accounting, Business/Public Management, Finance, Economics, Quantitative Analyses, or closely related field.

An equivalent combination of education, experience and training which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities may be considered.


EACH APPLICATION MUST INCLUDE INFORMATION THAT CLEARLY DEMONSTRATES THE ABOVE QUALIFICATIONS FOR THIS POSITION.


Additional Information


Salary Range Transparency: The salary range listed in this announcement reflects the anticipated offer range for this position. Offers made within this range are based on qualifications, experience, and internal equity.

Tentative Interview Dates: October 15, 2026. Please note that interview dates are subject to change and only selected candidates will receive confirmation and additional details.

Job Location: 9187 Central Ave, Capitol Heights, MD 20743

Conditions of Employment: Upon selection, the candidate must:
  • Meet all training and performance standards and demonstrate proficiency as required by the agency.
  • Wear and use agency protective apparel and equipment in the performance of their assigned duties, if applicable.
  • Successfully pass preemployment checks which may include reference checks, background investigations, and drug screenings, where applicable.
  • Be willing and able to serve as an essential employee. Essential employees are expected to report during standard or non-standard hours as operations necessitate, or during emergencies. Essential employees are expected to report or remain at work when other County employees are granted Administrative Leave.

ONLY ONLINE APPLICATIONS WILL BE ACCEPTED

Eligibility to Work: Under the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, an employer is required to hire only U.S. citizens and lawfully authorized alien workers. Applicants who are selected for employment will be required to provide and verify authorization to work in the United States without sponsorship.

This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S., only after an offer has been accepted and the Form I-9 is completed. For information on E-Verify, or if you believe the County has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at 888-897-7781 or visit their website at dhs.gov/E-Verify.

INTERNAL APPLICANTS: If you are a current Prince George's County Government employee and seeking a promotion, in accordance with Section 16-200 of the Personnel Law, you have the right to appeal a rejection rating within five (5) working days of receiving a rejection notice. Union employees should refer to their respective collective bargaining agreement and/or union representative for their grievance procedure.

title: Project Director - Roofing
description:
A Day in the Life of a Roofing Project Director

As a Project Director, you'll oversee roofing projects from initial planning through successful completion, ensuring work is delivered safely, efficiently, on schedule, and within budget. Your day may include coordinating with customers, field teams, subcontractors, vendors, and internal stakeholders to keep projects moving forward. You'll develop and manage project plans, schedules, budgets, and resources while monitoring progress and addressing challenges that arise throughout the project lifecycle. You'll also visit job sites, communicate project updates, review performance, and ensure work is completed according to customer expectations, contract requirements, and applicable safety and quality standards.

In this role, you'll provide leadership and direction across multiple roofing projects while keeping a close eye on scope, costs, timelines, and overall project performance. You'll work proactively to identify potential issues, develop solutions, and keep customers and project teams informed every step of the way. Success in this position requires strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced construction environment. If you're a hands-on project leader who takes pride in delivering quality work and building strong relationships, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on both project success and customer satisfaction.

Responsibilities:

  • Overall management of projects
  • Works with leadership to understand, evaluate, develop, and execute the scope of work
  • Solicits, receives, and approves proposals from subcontractors to perform work within budget
  • Assists with the collection of project documentation and presentation of backup needed to support the work performed/invoiced
  • Prepares project schedule, including job crew and sub-contractors schedule, according to the scope of work
  • Coordinates site visits with subcontractors to facilitate meetings/visits with clients, adjusters, and consultants to adjust scope and pricing
  • Maintains a daily log of conditions, activities, communications, and notable events
  • Fills in as needed when additional responsibilities/tasks need to be completed, including physical labor
  • Creates and maintains job activity paperwork, jobsite inventories, and prepares reports
  • Prepares all information for data entry into estimating software including but not limited to project details/notes
  • Proactively monitors and provides updates when there is risk of a project not meeting expected budget, gross profit margin, or schedule
  • Manage receipt and approval of change orders
  • Maintains clean and safe job site
  • Manages bids and RFP packages
  • Gathers all necessary field measurements/psychometrics calculations, notes, plans, photo documentation, materials, etc.
  • Produces estimates in Xactimate, T&M or other professional estimation tools
  • Selects, measures, and tracks metrics
  • Works with PMs to buy out projects to achieve projected margins
  • Develops scope letters and establishes ROM and burn rates
  • Communicates with clients, insurance companies and consultants regarding all aspects of the loss
  • Conducts audits and invoicing with leadership oversight
  • Negotiates claim settlements with leadership oversight
  • Collaborate with Operations Team on all projects to ensure estimating accuracy and buy in

Experience & Education:

  • Relevant leadership experience
  • 3 or more years' industry experience
  • Experience reading blueprints/architectural plans
  • Requires high-school diploma or equivalent

The Key Purpose of this role is to perform mechanical maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, installation, and inspection of plant and process equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation of production facilities. The Mechanical Process Artisan is responsible for maintaining equipment availability, minimizing downtime, and adhering to safety and quality standards.

Key Roles and Responsibilities:

Preventive and Corrective Maintenance

  • Carry out planned preventive maintenance on mechanical equipment and systems

  • Diagnose mechanical faults and perform corrective repairs on plant equipment

  • Inspect machinery and identify potential defects before failure occurs

  • Replace worn or damaged components in accordance with maintenance procedures

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records and reports

Equipment Installation and Repair

  • Install, align, and commission mechanical equipment

  • Repair pumps, compressors, conveyors, gearboxes, valves, piping systems, and other process plant machinery

  • Perform equipment overhauls and rebuilds as required

  • Ensure all repairs meet manufacturer specifications and company standards

Troubleshooting and Problem Solving

  • Investigate equipment breakdowns and determine root causes

  • Recommend and implement corrective actions to prevent recurring failures

  • Support continuous improvement initiatives aimed at increasing equipment reliability

Safety, Health, Environment and Quality (SHEQ)

  • Adhere to all company safety policies, procedures, and statutory regulations

  • Participate in risk assessments, toolbox talks, and safety inspections

  • Maintain good housekeeping standards in workshops and plant areas

  • Ensure that work permits, lockout/tagout procedures, and safety precautions are followed

Planning and Reporting

  • Complete job cards, maintenance reports, and inspection checklists

  • Report equipment defects, maintenance requirements, and safety concerns to supervisors

  • Assist in developing maintenance schedules and spare parts requirements

Teamwork and Communication

  • Work closely with operations personnel to minimize production interruptions

  • Support apprentices and trainees through knowledge sharing and coaching

  • Participate in maintenance meetings and improvement projects

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Equipment availability and reliability

  • Compliance with preventive maintenance schedules

  • Reduction in equipment downtime

  • Quality of maintenance work performed

  • Safety compliance and incident-free performance

  • Timely completion of assigned work orders

  • Maintenance cost control and efficient use of resources

Working Conditions

  • Work may be performed in workshops, processing plants, mining operations, or utility facilities

  • May require shift work, standby duties, and emergency callouts

  • Exposure to noise, dust, heat, and moving machinery

  • Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is mandatory

Key Attributes and Competencies:

  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills

  • Attention to detail

  • Good communication and interpersonal skills

  • Ability to work under pressure

  • Teamwork and collaboration

  • Problem-solving capability

  • Commitment to safety and quality

  • Time management and organizational skills

Minimum Requirements:

  • Certificate/Advanced Certificate in Mechanical Engineering

  • Grade 12 School Certificate or equivalent

  • Minimum 3 years' experience in industrial, manufacturing, mining, processing, or utility plant maintenance

  • Experience working on rotating and stationary equipment

  • Familiarity with CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management Systems) is an added advantage

title: Sr. Applied Scientist, Infrastructure Reliability
description:
Are you driven by innovation and complex problem-solving? At Infrastructure Reliability, we build scalable solutions that ensure the reliability of Amazon's critical systems. Our team develops and operates tools that detect and prevent outages to maintain high availability across Amazon's global infrastructure. Join us to architect solutions that directly impact millions of customers, with the resources and support to make meaningful contributions.

The team at Amazon is responsible for building intelligent and real-time insights into service-to-service communications, network traffic, and event correlation across hundreds of Amazon's critical fulfillment and robotics services. Our solutions support visibility into anomalous service behavior to prevent and quickly recover from incidents, ensuring high availability to keep the Customer Promise.

We are seeking a talented Senior Applied Scientist to invent the next generation of agentic observability solutions at Amazon scale. In this role, you will define, lead, and build the science behind intelligent systems that reason about complex network and infrastructure telemetry, autonomously detect anomalies, and drive automated remediation. You will own the scientific direction end to end, partnering closely with engineering, product, and Network Development Engineers to translate a long-term science vision into concrete research and delivery roadmaps.

Working backwards from the needs of our customers and operations teams, you will take the lead on ambiguous, high-impact problems where neither the problem nor the solution is well defined, and deliver production systems that improve infrastructure availability at scale. You will invent new methods, drive their adoption across multiple teams, and remain deeply hands-on with the hardest technical challenges.

Key job responsibilities
* Define and own the science vision for agentic observability, translating it into research and engineering roadmaps in partnership with product and engineering leaders.

* Build ML and agentic AI systems that autonomously detect, classify, and correlate infrastructure anomalies across network, compute, and service layers at Amazon scale.

* Design and develop models for event correlation, root cause analysis, and predictive failure detection using time-series analysis, graph-based methods, and deep learning.

* Own the agentic architecture for automated observability workflows, including planning, tool integration, long-horizon reasoning, and multi-agent orchestration.

* Define and curate the datasets and evaluation methodologies needed to train, benchmark, and continuously improve detection and classification systems.

* Stay deeply hands-on: write production-quality, critical-path code and build core components that take systems from prototype to launch.
Partner with Network Development Engineers and operations teams to ground science solutions in real-world infrastructure behavior and operational needs.

* Mentor scientists and engineers, raise the science bar, and represent the team in the internal and external scientific community through publications and presentations.

A day in the life
You will solve real-world problems by analyzing large-scale network telemetry and operational data, designing experiments and simulations, and developing ML models that detect and prevent infrastructure incidents. Your work requires close collaboration with engineers, Network Development Engineers, product managers, and operations leaders across the organization. You will prepare written and verbal presentations to share insights with audiences of varying technical sophistication, and you will iterate rapidly between research and production deployment.

title: Global Quality Control Director (Offshore)
description:
Job Overview:

Weatherford have an excellent opportunity for an experienced Global Quality Control Director (Offshore). The position will be based in downtown Houston, Texas.

The Global Quality Control Director provides global leadership, strategy, and governance for Quality Control across Weatherford’s Repair & Maintenance (R&M) and Offshore Services Operations. The role establishes and maintains global Quality Control standards, inspection and testing requirements, equipment release controls, measurement systems, and service-readiness processes to ensure products, equipment, and services consistently meet customer, regulatory, industry, and company requirements prior to release or use. Working closely with Quality, Engineering, Operations, Product Lines, and Geozone leadership, the position drives standardization, process discipline, and effective quality controls across the organization.

The role is accountable for governing inspection and verification programs, nonconformance and corrective action processes, calibration and measurement systems, quality performance metrics, and continuous improvement initiatives. Through the application of risk-based controls, data-driven decision making, and global quality governance, the Director identifies and mitigates systemic risks, prevents recurring failures, strengthens compliance with the Weatherford Management System and applicable API and ISO standards, and promotes a culture of prevention, operational excellence, and customer satisfaction across all Geozones.

Responsibilities:

OPERATIONS

Global Quality Control Strategy and Governance

  • Maintain the global R&M and Services Operations Quality Control strategy aligned with business priorities.
  • Set global minimum requirements, procedures, tools, records, terminology, and governance.
  • Standardize inspection, testing, status, acceptance, hold-point, release, and readiness practices across Geozones.
  • Control local adaptations for regulatory, customer, technical, or operational needs.
  • Own global Quality Control processes and tools.
  • Lead governance reviews of systemic risk, implementation, control effectiveness, recurring failures, and actions.

Inspection, Test and Verification Controls

  • Establish risk-based Inspection and Test Plan requirements with Engineering, Product Lines, Quality Assurance, customers, and technical standards.
  • Define acceptance criteria, critical characteristics, inspection stages, hold and witness points, responsibilities, records, and release authority.
  • Govern required receiving, in-process, final, functional, pressure, and performance inspections and tests.
  • Control nondestructive examination, independent verification, witnessing, and reinspection after correction or rework.
  • Maintain traceable inspection and test status linked to the asset, serial number, work order, traveler, or service record.
  • Standardize reports and objective evidence for independent conformity verification.27

Measurement, Calibration and Test Equipment

  • Govern measuring equipment used to inspect, test, verify, or release R&M and service equipment.
  • Set controls for identification, calibration, traceability, protection, storage, verification, and overdue or out-of-tolerance equipment.
  • Assess affected results when equipment is out of tolerance.
  • Monitor calibration compliance and recurring measurement risks.
  • Ensure measurement capability meets defined tolerances and acceptance criteria.

Equipment Release and Service Readiness

  • Establish risk-based release and readiness gates for R&M outputs, service assets, equipment, and records.
  • Define hold, release, exception, and no-go requirements before shipment, mobilization, job start or return to service.
  • Prevent critical-equipment release without complete inspection, testing, calibration, configuration, concession, preservation, and readiness evidence.
  • Require final record review, release status, traceability, equipment identification, and approved exceptions.
  • Convert readiness, operational control, risk, competency, spares, and lessons-learned requirements into verifiable evidence.
  • Monitor releases with open quality-critical items and escalate release-discipline failures.

NCR, CPAR and Corrective-Action Effectiveness

  • Govern nonconformance, corrective and preventive action, root cause, containment, disposition, and effectiveness.
  • Ensure timely identification, segregation, control, disposition, reinspection, approval, and closure of nonconforming outputs.
  • Scale root-cause analysis to severity, recurrence, complexity, and customer or operational impact.
  • Address underlying process, system, technical, supplier, competency, or organizational causes - not only defects.
  • Require evidence of action implementation and effectiveness before closure.
  • Govern repeat-failure coding, recurrence reviews, cross-Geozone trends, and systemic-risk escalation.
  • Convert lessons learned into controlled updates to procedures, plans, instructions, training, engineering, supplier controls, and readiness gates.

Quality Management System and Certification

  • Support implementation and continual improvement of the Weatherford Management System across R&M and Services Operations.
  • Ensure Quality Control supports applicable API Q1, API Q2, ISO 9001, customer, licensing, regulatory, and certification requirements.
  • Partner with the Quality Management System and Audit function on risk-based audits, certification readiness, findings, corrective actions, and compliance.
  • Support customer, certification-body, regulatory, and internal audits.
  • Provide Quality Control evidence and expertise for significant findings or certification risks.
  • Meet local requirements through approved controls without weakening global minimums.
  • API Q2 covers service supply, including repair and maintenance; API Q1 covers product organizations, including inspection, testing, servicing, and final acceptance. ISO 9001 defines quality management system requirements.

Performance, Improvement and Business Outcomes

  • Maintain a global scorecard of leading and lagging Quality Control indicators.
  • Analyze results by Geozone, facility, Product Line, equipment, process, defect, detection point, and recurring failure mode.
  • Prioritize improvements by safety and customer risk, severity, recurrence, nonproductive time, cost of poor quality, readiness, and business impact.
  • Lead cross-functional projects to eliminate recurring defects, strengthen release discipline and process capability, and prevent escapes.
  • Report performance, systemic risks, actions, progress, and outcomes to the GBL Quality Sr. Director and leadership.
  • Promote a prevention-based Quality culture that uses results, weak signals, failures, and lessons learned to improve controls and decisions.

SAFETY, SECURITY, ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE

  • Ensure ethical compliance with Weatherford governance, policies, the Management System, laws, standards, and Rules to Live By.
  • Prioritize Quality, safety, security, and environmental protection.
  • Use Stop Work Authority for unacceptable safety, quality, integrity, or nonconformance risk.
  • Ensure Quality Control meets customer, contractual, legal, regulatory, and certification requirements.
  • Promote open escalation of quality risks without retaliation or pressure to release nonconforming equipment or services.

COMMUNICATION

  • Serves and maintains effective communications with all key stakeholders both internal, including Quality, SVP Product Lines, Product Line, Global Service Delivery, and where appropriate external.
  • As requested by the VP PL or Quality VP, support client visits and constant communication to demonstrate our commitment and promote the Weatherford Quality and HSE process.

title: Systems Development Engineer , Frontier Amazon Dedicated Cloud (ADC)
description:
The Frontier ADC team is at the forefront of delivering the AWS GenAI and Agentic AI service portfolio to our customers in GovCloud and isolated environments. We are dedicated to pushing the boundaries of what is possible in this rapidly evolving field, leveraging the power of cloud computing and the latest advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies. With a focus on expanding Frontier AI services across GovCloud and isolated regions, driving automation investments, and delivering innovative solutions, we are at the forefront of modernization. Our teams are innovating new ways of building massively scalable distributed systems and delivering the next generation of cloud computing across the GenAI and Agentic AI service portfolio. We support the GenAI and Agentic AI service portfolio including services like Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Quick, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Kiro.

We are seeking a Systems Development Engineer II who can think big and simplify solutions to complex problems, all while ensuring our customers continue to have the best experience possible!

A successful Systems Development Engineer II joining the team will be an innovator, building solutions and working closely with Amazon's largest and most demanding government customers to address their specific needs across a suite of Frontier AI services in GovCloud and isolated environments. They will drive the resolution of technical issues and work diligently to improve the customer experience.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph. The position further requires the candidate to opt into a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate will:

• Be great fun to work with. Our company credo is "Work hard. Have fun. Make history". The right candidate will love what they do and instinctively know how to make work fun.

• Have strong Linux & Networking Fundamentals. The ideal candidate will have deep experience working with Linux, preferably in a large scale, distributed environment. You understand networking technology and how servers and networks inter-relate. You regularly take part in deep-dive troubleshooting and conduct technical post-mortem discussions to identify the root cause of complex issues.

• Have strong software and systems skills. The ideal candidate will have deep experience working with systems in a large scale, distributed environment. You understand networking technology and how servers and networks inter-relate. You are comfortable facilitating deep-dive troubleshooting and leading technical post-mortem discussions to identify the root cause of complex issues.

• Love to solve problems. The ideal candidate will love leading teams to solve difficult technical problems related to AWS service builds and operations in GovCloud and isolated environments. You have a solid understanding of systems design, operations, automation, and process improvement.

• Think Big. The ideal candidate will work on projects building and deploying solutions across GovCloud and isolated regions. You will strive to build a culture to improve and streamline processes to allow for work on a massive scale.

A day in the life
As a Systems Development Engineer II in Frontier ADC, you will build innovative solutions, expand services into GovCloud and isolated regions, and improve our operations to provide resiliency and the best experience for our customers. You influence technical strategy and architectural decisions within the team and with partner teams and make data-driven decisions. Successful candidates will be expected to show leadership on strong Bias for Action, Invent and Simplify, Insist on the Highest Standards, and Deliver Results.

You will develop, build, and operate AWS Frontier AI services that enable customers to leverage generative AI and agentic capabilities in secure environments. Our engineering teams support services running in GovCloud and isolated regions, creating unique engineering challenges and opportunities for innovation. The Frontier ADC team is responsible for diving deep to resolve operational challenges, innovating to automate operational tasks, building solutions for our customers, supporting execution of various security campaigns (blocked software, host patching), and parity programs.

As a Systems Development Engineer II you will:

• Work cross-functionally to foster a constructive dialogue, harmonize discordant views, and lead the resolution of contentious issues.

• Love to code. Whether it's building tools in Java or solving complex system problems in Python, the ideal candidate will love using technology to solve problems.

• Think Big. The ideal candidate will build and deploy solutions across thousands of devices. You will strive to improve and streamline processes to allow for work on a massive scale.

About the team
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

title: Project Coordinator Scaling Near Vision Glasses
description:
(Role is contingent on the receipt of the award)

This role was posted on September 17, 2026. Please note that we will review applications on a rolling basis.

About Last Mile Health

Last Mile Health saves lives in the world's most remote communities. Our vision is a health worker within reach of everyone, everywhere. We partner with governments to recruit, train, equip, and integrate professional community health workers into national health systems, equipping them to deliver quality primary care in rural and remote communities. Founded in Liberia in 2007, we now operate programs in Ethiopia, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Malawi. Our global offices are located in Accra, Ghana, and in the United States. We are looking for mission-driven leaders to join us as we work to ensure no patient is out of reach.

About the Liberia Team

Partnering with the Ministry of Health since 2007, the Liberia team pioneered the community health worker model that serves as a national blueprint. Originating in the remote Konobo District, their work demonstrated that professional community health workers could drastically increase health-seeking behavior and improve health outcomes, increasing skilled birth attendance from 55% to 84%. Led by Brittney Varpilah, the team champions a supervised, salaried, supplied, and skilled workforce to deliver primary care in the country’s hardest-to-reach regions. Beyond delivery, they strengthen health systems through high-level advocacy and policy design while upskilling the workforce through rigorous training and continuous quality improvement.

The Role

At Last Mile Health, we are all stewards of our reputation and resources. Do you have extensive experience and a proven track record of coordinating county-level health projects, upskilling health workers, and supporting eyeglasses distribution through the National Community Health Assistant (NCHA) Program? If so, then you may be our next Program Coordinator – Near Vision Scale-Up.

Building on Liberia’s Margibi County pilot and the inclusion of community eye-health services in the National Community Health Policy (2023-2033), the Program Coordinator will help translate the national policy and curriculum on eye health into consistent service delivery across nine counties. In partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Program Coordinator will lead the scale-up of reading glasses distribution to reach approximately 3000,000 people within two years.

By leveraging the already financed Community Health Assistants (CHAs) training, the Program Coordinator will work with the MOH and relevant partners to ensure the integration of advocacy, vision Monitoring and Evaluation Systems, and continuous learning as an integrated component of near vision service delivery. Ultimately, the Program Coordinator aims to improve the lives and livelihoods of thousands of Liberians who currently lack access to vision screening and eyeglasses.

This position is on-site and based in Monrovia, Liberia, and is only open to candidates who are Liberian nationals currently located in Liberia.

Duration: 24 Months

What You’ll Do

Field Implementation and continuous technical support

  • Provide continuous technical support to trained personnel at national, county, district, and community levels to ensure consistent and high-quality implementation.
  • Support National, County, and District stakeholders throughout the distribution process, including planning, implementation, and follow-up.
  • Implement and monitor quality assurance mechanisms across screening and distribution activities, including adherence to clinical protocols, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and data accuracy standards.
  • Plan, coordinate, and oversee institution-based near-vision screening activities in Montserrado County, working with MOH, higher learning education institutions, and relevant partners to organize screening, dispensing of reading glasses, referrals, and follow-up.
  • Coordinate the deployment and equitable distribution of near-vision glasses, ensuring efficient logistics and client satisfaction.

Training, Supportive Supervision, Monitoring, and Evaluation

  • Coordinate and support refresher training for CHAs to reinforce competencies in near-vision screening, appropriate dispensing of glasses, referral, and adherence to established NCHA eye health protocols.
  • Plan, coordinate, and support quarterly integrated supervision visits to the project implementation counties to assess the quality of near-vision screening and service delivery, referral practices, commodity management, data quality, and adherence to established NCHA Program protocols. Visits will include verification, data validation, quality control, and general oversight.
  • In collaboration with the MERL Specialist, support data entry and management using standardized tracking tools to ensure timely, accurate, and complete data capture and facilitate feedback collection and sharing for continuous program improvement.
  • Provide technical support for adaptation and implementation of decision-support tools and their integration into routine workflows and supervision systems.
  • Support implementation-learning, costing and cost modeling, evaluation, and knowledge management activities to inform continuous improvement, sustainability, cost reduction, and future national scale-up.

Advocacy, demand generation, and stakeholder coordination

  • Plan and coordinate advocacy activities at the Ministry of Health, Subnational (County Health Teams), district, and community levels to raise awareness and generate demand for near vision glasses among populations in need.
  • Build and maintain strong working partnerships with the Ministry of Health (MoH), County Health Teams, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to sustain the momentum for investment in near vision correction and vision glasses availability.
  • Actively participate in technical working groups (TWGs) and coordination forums to share updates, align strategies, and promote learning.

Participate in additional Programs or cross-team activities, as requested

  • Actively participate in the LMH Liberia program’s internal team technical working group meetings
  • Support other emerging Programs team needs as determined by the manager.

What you’ll bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree with experience in the field of public health, Nursing, Community Health, Health Services Management.
  • An optometrist background is an additional advantage
  • Relevant professional experience in one or more of the work areas highlighted in the job summary.
  • Demonstrated experience working within the national and/or sub-national health system (community health workers program a plus); familiarity with government structures and processes
  • Demonstrated experience working in primary health care interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Community Health Information System and DHIS2
  • Ability to diplomatically navigate complex stakeholder dynamics, proactively solve problems, and achieve results and consensus with multiple influencers.
  • Demonstrated experience in partner engagement and project management.
  • Comfortable working in teams as well as acting independently in the implementation of specific tasks, prioritizing, working under pressure, and meeting deadlines.
  • Robust knowledge management skills, including the advanced use of MS Office applications and Google Suite.

You’ll impress us if you have

  • Digital health program design or implementation experience
  • Facilitation of training/capacity strengthening for adult learners
  • Knowledge on application of AI for health service delivery
  • Knowledge of existing data being tracked in DHIS2, specifically community health data.
  • Experience implementing an advocacy agenda with national and subnational government stakeholders​​​​.

We're looking for someone with many of the qualifications listed above, but we know no one meets every requirement. If you're excited about our mission and believe your experience aligns with this role, we encourage you to apply.

Compensation information

At Last Mile Health, we are committed to equitable and transparent compensation. Employees are paid using a clear, consistent methodology that is fully transparent and accessible to everyone. We look forward to answering any questions you may have during the hiring process. Before applying to this role, please take a moment to learn more about our approach to compensation and how compensation works in each of the countries where we operate.
