title: Social Educator
description:
Harmeny Education Trust is a charitable organisation providing therapeutic care and education to children who have experienced early years trauma through abuse, neglect and family disruption, referred from all over Scotland. We currently work with children and young people aged 5-18, both on a day and all-year-round residential basis.
We are currently seeking a Social Educator to join our Education Team on a part-time, fixed-term basis, with the primary focus of providing dedicated 1-to-1 support for a pupil within the formal education setting.

This post is initially until 2 July 2027; the fixed-term element of the contract is determined by local authority funding, and will remain under review, with the possibility of extension following review.

The role centres on meeting the individual needs of the pupil, supporting their learning, and promoting meaningful engagement within the classroom and other learning environments.

The post holder will be able to plan and offer therapeutic experiences to individual children and small groups across the education and care setting, providing a strong link to the residential cottages and building relationships with parents, carers and families.

The successful applicant will be required to work 32 hours per week during term time only. This position is term-time based, with no requirement to work during school holidays. Annual leave will be taken within agreed term-time arrangements. The working pattern for this post is: Monday to Thursday 8.30am-3.30pm, Friday 8.30am-12.30pm term-time only.

The successful candidate will be appointed on the Harmeny salary scale, at a point between 11 and 15 (£29,866 to £32,600) depending on qualifications and experience. The pro rata salary for this role will be £24,155 to £26,366.

The successful candidate will be required to join the Protecting Vulnerable Groups (PVG) Scheme and register with the Scottish Social Services Council (SSSC).
A driving licence allowing the use of our vehicles is essential.
Harmeny is a values-led organisation and a good fit with our ethos is as important to us as having relevant experience.
Harmeny is situated in a beautiful 35-acre woodland estate, which includes residential and education accommodation, community garden, orchard, wildlife habitats and children’s play areas. Harmeny is located in Balerno on the outskirts of Edinburgh, at the foot of the Pentland Hills; we are easily accessible by bus and there is on-site parking available.
We offer benefits and opportunities that promote wellbeing, work-life balance and staff development. Benefits include:
  • On-site wellbeing spaces and free massage therapy
  • Free gym membership & psychotherapeutic support
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Access to a wellbeing app and counselling
  • Access to discounts on shopping and events.
  • Access to a comprehensive induction package, and to a range of learning and development opportunities throughout their career with us.
More information on the benefits of working at Harmeny, plus a fuller job description and person specification can be found at www.harmeny.org.uk/jobs.

If you are interested in joining our dynamic team, please contact Cassie Gaughan, Service Manager, on 0131 449 3938.
To apply, please complete the application form via our recruitment section at www.harmeny.org.uk/jobs.

Closing date: 2 October 2026

Key areas of the job
  1. Working closely with the Class Teacher and Education Teams, the post holder will contribute to the provision of the highest quality learning experiences and outcomes for children placed at Harmeny, which is based on a relational and experiential model of learning.
  2. The post holder will contribute to a culture and ethos within a highly nurturing and supporting environment, in order to provide the secure base that children require to engage in their learning.
  3. Alongside providing learning support and promoting engagement with learning within the classroom, they will also play a key role in supporting those aspects of the 24-hour curriculum which assist children in developing their social skills, as vital components for lifelong learning.
  4. With the supervision and guidance of the Service Manager (Education Support), the post holder will be responsible alongside the Class Teacher Team to identify specific needs of the children within the class and take the lead on regular direct work that helps support the children’s social and emotional development, based on an understanding of the key principles of Attachment, Resilience, Child Development and Trauma Informed Care.
Principle responsibilities
  1. Promote a positive ethos in the school consistent with Harmeny’s vision, purpose and core values.
  2. Support the Education Management Team (EMT) with the implementation of the School Improvement Plan, Harmeny Strategic Plan and Harmeny policies and procedures.
  3. Be an integral part of the Education team and develop solid working partnerships with the wider Harmeny community.
  4. Provide support to children during transitions throughout the school day and support individuals outwith the classroom when agreed by EMT.
  5. Communicate with education and care colleagues, parents/carers and a range of other professionals to ensure coherent working and positive outcomes for children.
  6. Communicate and interact positively with children using solution-focussed & strengths-based principles in line with Harmeny policies, procedures and core values.
  7. Develop and implement care plans as part of the child’s key team, which address the needs of the child.
  8. Involved in the development and implementation of risk assessment planning for children.
  9. Implement physical intervention techniques (where required).
  10. Provide learning support within the classroom and other environments, following the guidance of Classroom Teachers and EMT.
  11. Promote children’s engagement with learning, through building positive relationships and encouraging children to remain ‘on task’.
  12. Support the delivery of the curriculum, specifically designed to meet the individual educational, care and therapeutic needs of children, in line with national policies such as CfE and GIRFEC.
  13. Deliver direct individual or group work as guided by the Service Manager (Education Support) or EMT.
  14. Prepare classroom teaching resources, maintain audio-visual and ICT equipment and assist with the layout and tidiness of the classroom.
  15. Ensure whole-school educational equipment, resources and spaces are maintained to an excellent standard, with responsibility for overseeing a specific resource area.
  16. Provide administrative support, including the maintenance of accurate records, filing and photocopying.
  17. Support the development of children’s Personal Learning Planning and help children work towards individual goals and targets.
  18. Gather evidence for individual plans and through preparation of displays.
  19. As a valued member of a child’s key team, participate in regular reviews and submit written reports on individual children as requested.
  20. Attend regular staff meetings as required. To ensure that all children’s personal records are kept up to date within the database.
  21. Be flexible within the timetable and working patterns at the discretion of the Service Manager (Education Support) or EMT.
  22. Attend supervision, APR, training and other meetings as required.
  23. Participate in residential trips and holidays when required.
  24. Safely drive children and staff to and from outings, activities and external meetings via minibus or fleet vehicle.
  25. To undertake any other duties as delegated by ELT or SLT which are consistent with the role of Social Educator.
  26. To ensure that the highest possible standards of professional practice are maintained
Essential:
  1. A relevant qualification in Social Care in line with the Scottish Social Services Council (the SSSC) registration requirements for Residential Child Care Workers (e.g. HNC, SVQ, etc.)
  2. Knowledge and understanding of children who are Looked After and Accommodated and children with complex Additional Support Needs.
  3. Ability to contribute to raising the standards of attainment and achievement for children with complex Additional Support Needs.
  4. Knowledge of child development, childcare legislation, the Scottish curriculum and relevant policies and procedures.
  5. Knowledge of the residential childcare sector.
  6. A working knowledge of the Curriculum for Excellence.
  7. Understanding of children’s behaviour and need to encourage positive and appropriate behaviours, through the use of effective strategies which recognise the complex behaviours of children at Harmeny.
  8. Experience in residential work and / or childcare and / or within an education setting.
  9. Understanding of the ‘duty of care’ to children and colleagues.
  10. Understanding of the practice issues of ‘physical intervention’ and ability to undertake such physical intervention when required.
  11. Experience, skill and commitment to working within a multi-disciplinary setting.
  12. A commitment to Children’s Rights and participation of children and their families.
  13. Good communication skills, both written and oral.
  14. Good organisational and administrative skills and computer literate.
  15. A full driving licence and the ability to drive fleet vehicles and transport children as required.
Desirable:
  1. Evidence of further training in therapeutic work with children and young people.
  2. Knowledge of social pedagogical approach.
  3. Knowledge and experience of organising and delivering children’s activities/group work and/or supporting children’s learning.
Personal Characteristics / Competencies:
  1. A commitment to the needs of children who are Looked after, accommodated and have complex additional support needs.
  2. Able to appropriately communicate with children, colleagues, families and external professionals.
  3. Ability to work within a team and demonstrate appropriate autonomy to meet the demands of both the practical direct support and recording/reporting requirements in a highly pressurised working environment.
  4. Demonstrates emotional intelligence, understands the needs of others, and personal resilience.
  5. Proactive and takes the initiative to gain the information needed for the role, with a flexible and ‘can do’ attitude.
  6. Commitment to continuous improvement.
  • Competitive salary
  • Pension scheme
  • Life assurance scheme (three times salary)
  • Enhanced pay for maternity, adoption and paternity leave
  • Policies and practices that promote health and wellbeing, including massage therapy and access to a wellbeing space
  • We are highly committed to the professional development of all our staff and the post-holders will have access to comprehensive training and development opportunities

title: PROBATION AND PAROLE OFFICER 1, 2, or 3- Adult
description:
About this Job


Louisiana Department of Public Safety & Corrections –
Corrections Services

Division of Probation & Parole – Adult

MONROE DISTRICT

Ouachita, Louisiana



Our Mission

The mission of Corrections Services is to enhance public safety through the safe and secure incarceration of offenders, effective probation/parole supervision, and proven rehabilitative strategies that successfully reintegrate offenders into society, as well as to assist individuals and communities victimized by crime. Goals and priorities are built around the Department’s commitment to public safety and rehabilitation and serve to guide our performance in carrying out our mission. Goals and priorities include: staff and offender safety, provision of basic services, opportunity for change, opportunity for making amends, and reentry.


Make a difference in your community as a Probation and Parole Officer. In this impactful role, you will supervise and investigate criminal offenders while promoting public safety, accountability, and successful rehabilitation through probation, parole, and pardon services. If you are motivated by service and thrive in a fast-paced criminal justice environment, this career is for you.

Why work for DOC?

  • Culture: DOC values and supports employees through numerous recognition programs, creating a sense of community, prioritizing internal promotional opportunities, clear communication, and professional development.
  • Growth: Professional growth is encouraged at DOC through numerous avenues.
  • Benefits: DOC offers a generous benefits package including; a defined benefit pension plan, health insurance that is also available post retirement, at least 10 paid holidays, sick and annual leave that rolls over from year to year, paid or time off accrued for hours worked over 40 per week, a deferred compensation plan, a flexible benefits plan, alternate work schedules etc. Alternative work schedules, including 4/10’s MAY be an available benefit for certain positions upon meeting the policy requirements.

AN IDEAL CANDIDATE SHOULD POSSESS THE FOLLOWING COMPETENCIES:
  • Driving Results: The ability to set and pursue goals, maintain focus amid competing demands, and deliver results.
  • Following Policies and Procedures: The ability to follow, reinforce, adapt, or develop policies and procedures to maintain compliance with federal and state legal requirements, State Civil Service rules, and organizational policies.
  • Making Accurate Judgments: The ability to assess options, weigh risks, and make sound decisions using available information and logical reasoning.

Minimum Qualifications

Three years of experience in corrections or law enforcement; OR

Three years of continuous active military duty (all Military Occupational Specialties apply); OR

Six years of full-time experience in any field; OR

A bachelor's degree.

EXPERIENCE SUBSTITUTION:
Every 30 semester hours earned from an accredited college or university will be credited as one year of experience towards the six years of full-time work experience in any field. The maximum substitution allowed is 120 semester hours which substitutes for a maximum of four years of experience in any field.

NECESSARY SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:
An applicant who has been convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence or a felony, or who is under indictment on a felony charge will be disqualified until relief from the disabilities imposed by state and federal laws is granted.

Possession of a current Louisiana driver's license.

This position requires the incumbent to handle and carry firearms.

Willingness and ability to attain a Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST) certification.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

  • Supervise felony and misdemeanor offenders through counseling, case management, and referrals to community resources that support rehabilitation and social adjustment.
  • Enforce conditions of probation and parole by monitoring compliance, managing violations, and participating in all stages of the violation process.
  • Conduct criminal justice investigations and prepare reports and recommendations for courts, parole and pardon boards, and other criminal justice decision makers.
  • Conduct arrests, transport violators, and participate in probable cause, revocation, and disciplinary hearings.
  • Investigate and manage restitution, supervision fees, fines, court costs, and other criminal justice-related financial obligations.
  • Coordinate offender placement in drug treatment, vocational rehabilitation, mental health, and other support programs while providing crisis intervention and emergency assistance resources.
  • Administer drug testing, supervise community service activities, and ensure compliance with American Correctional Association (ACA) standards and agency policies.
  • Assist with jail and contract compliance audits for facilities and Community Rehabilitation Centers (CRCs), including applying defensive tactics and maintaining institutional safety and security.

Position-Specific Details:

Appointment Type: Probational or Promotion of a permanent, classified employee of the Louisiana State Government.

  • Current permanent status classified state employees may be required to accept a probational appointment if accepted.
  • An employee selected for a promotion may be required to serve a trial detail prior to being permanently promoted.
  • This posting may also be used to fill a vacancy as a temporary job appointment. If filled as a temporary job appointment, should a permanent position become available, the employee may be converted to a probational appointment.

Career Progression: This position may be filled as a Probation and Parole Officer 1, 2, or 3, depending on the level of experience of the selected applicant.

Compensation:
Special Entrance Rates:
The Probation and Parole Officer 1-Adult has a Special Entrance Rate of $1,872.00 Bi-weekly.
The Probation and Parole Officer 2-Adult has a Special Entrance Rate of $2,003.20 Bi-weekly.
The Probation and Parole Officer 3-Adult has a Special Entrance Rate of $2,213.60 Bi-weekly.

Other Important Information:
  • This Agency is a Drug-Free Workplace.
  • Any degree, certificate, special license, or DD-214 must be verified by official documentation prior to hire.
  • Any qualifying experience that is based on college credit/college hours should have an accompanying transcript for verification.

Louisiana is a State As a Model Employer (SAME) that supports the recruitment, hiring, and retention of individuals with disabilities.

How To Apply:

No Civil Service Test Score is required in order to be considered for this vacancy.

To apply for this vacancy, click on the “Apply” link above and complete an electronic application, which can be used for this vacancy as well as future job opportunities. Applicants are responsible for checking the status of their application to determine where they are in the recruitment process. Further status message information is located under the Information section of the Current Job Opportunities page.

*Information to support your eligibility for the position must be included in the application (i.e., relevant, detailed experience/education). Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of completed education and experience sections. Applications may be rejected if incomplete.

To view and apply to any of our other postings we currently have available, click HERE.

The Louisiana Department of Public Safety and Corrections - Corrections Services is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on any non-merit factor, including disability.


For more information about this vacancy, contact:
Brittany Decook
Division of Adult Probation and Parole
P.O. Box 94304
Baton Rouge, LA 70804-9304
Brittany.Decook@la.gov

title: Part-Time Community Associate, 800 N High Street
location: Columbus, OH United States of America
description:
About Us

At WeWork, we provide flexible workspace solutions to help businesses of all sizes thrive in more than 37 countries worldwide. The future of work is here, and we’re not just a part of that movement—we’re leading it. United by a desire to build a global community, our purpose is to give members the support to do their best work, and the space to take their ideas to new heights. Join us as we empower tomorrow’s world at work.

Community Associate | Community

About the Opportunity

As a Community Associate, you'll be the primary point of contact for the Community and act as the “face” of WeWork! You will report to your building each day to support the Community Management team.

Your work, which will include but not be limited to the duties listed below, will help WeWork to achieve the following:

  • Build a welcoming and collaborative community environment amongst our members through events and building relationships between members!

  • Ensure that your building is fully operational and processes are running efficiently.

  • Drive growth and promotion of WeWork-provided service offerings.

  • Take direction from the Community Lead and the Community Manager to support the Community Team as necessary.

  • All of this while illustrating WeWork’s core values and working towards achieving our mission.

Depending on the location you are assigned, you’ll either work with a variety of members from different backgrounds and industries, or focus your efforts on one of our Enterprise clients. Employees supporting our Enterprise locations may have different holidays, technical systems, operational and relationship requirements, and property management responsibilities than employees in our Classic locations.

In this role, you’ll be responsible for the following areas:

Front Desk Management:

  • Cover the front desk during the building’s set business hours and be an on-site point of contact, easily located on the member floor or at Community Bar.

  • Greet members and guests with a warm and welcoming demeanor.

  • Ensure all visiting guests are in accordance with WeWork's guest policy by ensuring all guests properly sign-in via Welkio tablet.

  • Learn the names of members and guests with the goal of building relationships in order to facilitate the sense of Community WeWork is known for.

  • Anticipate member and guest needs before they arise using relevant information collected about members to enhance and personalize their experience.

  • Ensure building Specific forms are up to date including pet forms, filming requests, bike room requests, etc.

  • Keep the front desk clean and organized.

  • Notify members of any food deliveries and couriers.

  • Answer any questions from members and guests related to the building including way-finding, policies and procedures, community etiquette, etc.

Events and Membership Engagement:

  • Provide feedback on programming types (based on member makeup) and evaluate events based on attendance, satisfaction, and impact on the appropriate event team.

  • Consistently celebrate members’ successes and milestones through gifts and notes.

  • Distribute all necessary info to promote the event including creation and posting of weekly events poster and individual event posters.

  • Ensure building-specific operational requirements are met for each event (elevators, HVAC, etc).

  • Input notes into Kube or equivalent system about Members.

  • Identify and execute opportunities to connect members with each other.

  • Know and recommend local restaurants, food delivery services, catering options, team outing venues, post office, shipping center, supply store, etc.

  • Be active on the WeWork member network to engage members.

  • Know and explain WeWork policies and procedures and communicate, inform, and update members on building issues.

  • Ensure music levels and activations are appropriate to the daypart and occasion.

  • Write and send broadcasts relating to building updates.

Building Operations and Management:

  • Receive, process, sort, and organize all mail.

  • Locate and issue posts via the regional system to members upon request.

  • Keep the mailroom organized and clean.

  • “Return to Sender" for unidentified mail and former member mail after 30 days of no-pick up.

  • Ensure courier parcels have all the correct details for scheduled pick-ups.

  • Investigate, escalate, and resolve 'lost' packages.

  • Know and explain WeWork policies and procedures around mail and mailroom.

  • Track, audit, and organize keys collected and distributed.

  • Manage keycard stock and request new inventory as needed.

  • Collect keys and key cards upon move-out.

  • Review location and how to use each piece of Emergency Equipment.

  • Provide support for an automated coffee machine for guests and members.

About You

We’d love to hear from you if you meet the qualifications below:

  • College graduate with a four-year degree preferred, but not required

  • 1+ years of hospitality experience

  • Customer service and/or sales experience a plus

  • Must have strong verbal and written communication skills

  • Outstanding interpersonal and multitasking skills

  • Demonstrate integrity, dependability, responsibility, accountability, self-awareness, work ethic, and compassion

  • Passion for entrepreneurial communities

  • Passion and understanding of WeWork’s mission and values

  • Proficient in basic computer skills

Compensation & Benefits

Base Pay: $20.50 - $22.50

Incentive Compensation: WeWork employees are eligible to participate in an incentive plan specific to their role. Your recruiter will detail what incentive plan is applicable to this specific role. WeWork incentive plans are subject to the terms of the applicable incentive compensation plan, which will be made available to you after commencing employment. WeWork reserves the right to amend its incentive plans, and nothing in this job requisition or any other document creates a right to a specific incentive plan payment.

Benefits: Part-time employees are eligible to participate in WeWork’s benefit plans and programs in effect from time to time, as made available to similarly situated employees, including paid sick time, paid parental leave, unpaid public holidays, and eligibility to participate in 401(k) plan.

Life at WeWork

Being a WeWorker is more than just a job. We believe the magic of work is sparked by the passion you bring, the places you go, the people you meet and the purpose you follow. And it starts here. Here you will brush shoulders with those who dare to dream and do. Here you will be welcomed by a community that embraces and inspires you—because together we can achieve more. Here we challenge ideas, and explore new ways of getting things done. Whether you are part of our Employee Community Groups, or part of a global project, we ask you to bring your open-minded attitude and collaborative spirit. In return, you will be part of a team where your unique perspectives are celebrated.

WeWork is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil status, pregnancy (or pregnancy-related conditions), gender identity or expression, transgender status or gender reassignment, race, color, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, religion or religious beliefs, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including genetic testing and characteristics), military or veteran status, or any other grounds or characteristic that is protected under the law. WeWork is also proud to be an affirmative action employer with respect to veterans and individuals with disabilities.

title: Supervisor, Application Development
description:
Old Republic Bitco is seeking an Application Development Supervisor to join our home office located in Davenport, IA. As a respected specialty insurer with 11 branch offices across 10 states, OR Bitco delivers tailored insurance solutions to complex industries such as construction, forest products, and oil and gas.

This position is open to hybrid work arrangement, blending flexibility with meaningful in-person collaboration.

At OR Bitco, our work is guided by core values. We care deeply about our people, partners, and customers. We are committed to excellence and accountability. We deliver on our promises with integrity and precision, and we strive to make a meaningful impact in everything we do. These values drive our mission to protect the people and industries that keep America running.

Join the OR Bitco team and be part of a workplace built on collaboration, open communication, and a positive culture that supports growth and success. If you are passionate about operational excellence and ready to make a measurable impact within a growing, industry-leading organization, OR Bitco offers the platform and challenge you have been seeking.

Position Summary:

As an Application Development Supervisor, you will lead and support the day-to-day delivery of software development across both strategic project initiatives and production support. You’ll play a key role in turning IT strategy into high-quality, scalable, and maintainable technology solutions while helping drive accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

You will provide both technical and people leadership, actively contributing to development efforts while guiding a team of developers, including employees and onshore/offshore consultants. You’ll help prioritize work, manage workloads, maintain a healthy development pipeline, and ensure your team follows established SDLC standards and delivers solutions that align with business priorities.

Working collaboratively across the enterprise, you’ll partner with business analysts, architects, and business and IT stakeholders to clarify requirements, implement effective solutions, and support successful deployments. You’ll also help maintain production stability, improve development processes, and create an environment where your team can grow, perform, and deliver meaningful results.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Partner with Application Development leadership to oversee the execution of software development and production support activities, including workload planning, capacity management, prioritization, work assignment, and delivery coordination to meet business objectives, project commitments, and established service levels.
  • Lead, coach, and develop software developers through performance management, mentoring, feedback, and career development activities, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
  • Build and sustain a high-performing, collaborative team through recruiting, onboarding, retention, continuous feedback, professional development, and the promotion of organizational values, department culture, and enterprise goals.
  • Serve as a management representative by communicating organizational priorities, promoting departmental culture and values, fostering positive employee relations, supporting change initiatives, and ensuring alignment between team activities and enterprise objectives.
  • Support effective delivery by translating business requirements into actionable development work, validating estimates, tracking progress, managing incidents, enhancements, and defects, and communicating performance metrics related to delivery, quality, responsiveness, and operational effectiveness.
  • Monitor and communicate team performance, development progress, code quality, production support responsiveness, application health, risks, constraints, and operational metrics while driving continuous improvements to ensure successful delivery of business objectives.
  • Actively contribute to the development team by participating in software development, analysis, troubleshooting, and technical implementation activities supporting project delivery, departmental objectives, and continuous improvement initiatives while balancing supervisory responsibilities for approximately 40% of the role.
  • Provide technical leadership through solution and code reviews, troubleshooting complex issues, mentoring team members, and establishing and enforcing development standards, non-functional requirements, SDLC practices, documentation standards, and change management processes that deliver scalable, reliable, and high-performing solutions.
  • Partner with QA, UAT, and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are properly tested, documented, deployed, and supported while meeting expectations for production availability, stability, monitoring, and supportability.
  • Partner with business analysts, architects, quality assurance teams, business stakeholders, and technology partners to ensure requirements are clearly defined, solutions are effectively implemented, and business and operational objectives are achieved.
  • Foster a data-first mindset throughout solution delivery by emphasizing real-time integrations, partnering with data engineering and analytics teams, and driving continuous improvement in processes, tooling, automation, monitoring, and engineering practices.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

title: Fleet Safety Lead
description:
Location: Hybrid – Preferably at a Large Climate Pros’ Branch Location

Glendale Heights, IL; Grand Prairie, TX; Lithia Springs, GA

At Climate Pros, we take pride in doing the job right, taking care of each other, and putting safety first. Join a team that values hard work, integrity, and craftsmanship while providing the training, support, and opportunities to build a long-term career.

Position Summary

We are seeking a knowledgeable and proactive Fleet Safety Lead to lead and continuously improve vehicle safety across our nationwide operations. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and sustaining a best-in-class fleet safety program for approximately 1,500 company vehicles, primarily medium-duty vans and pickup trucks. The successful candidate will possess extensive experience delivering driver training, coaching field employees, analyzing fleet performance data, and partnering with operational leadership to reduce vehicle collisions and strengthen a culture of safe driving.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of the company's fleet safety strategy
  • Champion a culture where safe vehicle operation is recognized as a professional responsibility and an essential condition of employment
  • Develop standardized fleet safety policies, procedures, and safe driving expectations
  • Establish consistent driver qualification, onboarding, and refresher training programs
  • Evaluate fleet risks and implement corrective actions to reduce vehicle incidents
  • Evaluate leading indicator data including vehicle telematics and implement preventative actions to mitigate risk in advance of an accident
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives using fleet performance data and collision trends
  • Lead or participate in investigations for all fleet accidents and implement effective corrective actions where applicable
  • Deliver classroom and hands-on driver training throughout the United States
  • Conduct in-vehicle evaluations, participate in ride-alongs, and perform field observations to reinforce safe driving behaviors for Technicians, and train select personnel at various Branches to do the same
  • Provide coaching on defensive driving, parking lot safety, backing operations, lane changes, speed management, following distance, hazard recognition, distracted driving prevention, adverse weather driving, fatigue awareness, and vehicle operation regulatory requirements
  • Develop consistent driver coaching and accountability processes following preventable vehicle incidents, including individualized improvement plans
  • Develop and implement engaging training programs using real-world collision case studies, industry best practices, driver performance metrics, incident trends, and adult learning principles for initial and ongoing training activities
  • Develop and deliver ongoing fleet safety communications including Safety Alerts, driving safety campaign materials, Safety Minutes, and other similar driver awareness initiatives
  • Develop, monitor, and communicate key performance indicators and leading metrics that measure the effectiveness of the fleet safety program
  • Support compliance with applicable FMCSA regulations, driver qualification requirements, CDL programs, and vehicle safety initiatives as applicable

Qualifications

  • Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible fleet safety experience
  • Experience supporting multiple geographically dispersed locations
  • Experience delivering classroom and behind-the-wheel driver training
  • Experience in developing safety procedures and training materials
  • Experience managing fleet safety programs for 1500+ vehicles preferred
  • Strong knowledge of defensive driving principles
  • Experience conducting collision investigations
  • Experience analyzing fleet safety metrics and telematics data
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong presentation and facilitation skills
  • Valid driver's license with exceptional driving record

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

  • Combination of office and field environments
  • Ability to operate company vehicles for training purposes
  • Ability to sit or drive for extended periods
  • Ability to enter and exit work vans and pickup trucks repeatedly
  • 20%-60% travel to Branches, customers sites, or project sites as required
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions during field observations

Key Competencies

  • Advanced understanding of defensive driving techniques
  • Strong instructional and adult learning skills
  • Excellent coaching and mentoring abilities
  • Ability to influence operational leaders
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to interpret telematics and dash camera data
  • Strong report writing skills
  • Experience using Microsoft Office Suite
  • Ability to develop professional training presentations
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Strong organizational and time management skills
  • Comfortable presenting to both executive leadership and field employees

Performance Expectations

  • Reducing preventable fleet collisions
  • Improving driver coaching completion rates
  • Increasing leading indicator performance
  • Developing standardized driver training across all Branches
  • Strengthening operational ownership of fleet safety
  • Improving telematics utilization
  • Building a sustainable fleet safety culture

Compensation within the stated range will vary based on the candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Final offers will be tailored to the individual’s qualifications and potential contribution.

$95-$105K

title: Investment Analyst, Special Operations, LAC Region
description: At the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. In fiscal year 2026, IFC committed a record $105.6 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries. For more information, visit www.ifc.org. The successful candidate will join IFC's Special Operations Department (CSO), which is part of the Risk Management Vice-presidency. The Risk Finance Vice Presidency Unit (CRFVP) helps to ensure that IFC is sufficiently profitable and capitalized to sustain and grow its operations through prudent risk management at the corporate, portfolio, project, and client levels. It sets best practice standards in risk management to drive sustainable private sector development in emerging markets. CRFVP works in partnership with other IFC Vice Presidents to ensure IFC meets its corporate objectives. The Department of Special Operations (CSO) is housed within CRFVP. Its primary responsibility is to resolve the problems and special issues in IFC's portfolios related to debt, equity, quasi-equity, and other types of investment instruments, and to optimize the Corporation's overall return on a net present value basis (including for B-loan Participants) while minimizing reputational risk and, where possible, maximizing developmental impact. CSO is seeking to recruit an Investment Analyst to be based in the IFC office in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The selected candidate will be an integral part of project teams and given high levels of responsibility and broad exposure to many aspects of CSO’s work. Some travel may be required. Duties and Accountabilities: The Investment Analyst will, inter-alia: • Review and analyze financial models. • Perform company financial analysis from a credit perspective. • Draft memoranda, reports, presentations, and other documentation required for IFC internal supervision processes. • Engage with staff from other departments (including Industry teams, Legal, Financial Operations, Credit, Syndications, etc.) as well as with clients and co-lenders in connection to project work. • Conduct industry and market research. • Participate in restructuring/rescheduling and investment recovery negotiations. • Support the selection, procurement, and engagement of financial and restructuring advisors. • Maintain CSO knowledge management platforms, ensuring that project and other information is complete and up to date. • Support the preparation of internal and external presentations, seminar materials, and knowledge sharing events.

title: Senior Program Manager III, Quick Commerce - 3PL Integration
description:
Amazon’s Quick Commerce organization is exploring a new operating model to expand our network and deliver everyday essentials to customers faster. We are seeking a Senior Program Manager to develop and lead our third-party integration strategy, creating a scalable model that enables external partners to secure, launch, and operate Quick Commerce sites.

This role will own the development of the 3P business plan and proposal, including operating models, financial requirements, partner capabilities, risk assessments, and the mechanisms required to scale. The Senior Program Manager will work across Global Procurement Operations (GPO), Finance, Legal, Operations, Real Estate, Product, and other partner teams to evaluate external benchmarks, assess model trade-offs, and define the path from initial pilot through broader network expansion.

The ideal candidate can move between strategy and execution. They will build detailed business cases, evaluate complex financial and operational trade-offs, and translate ambiguity into a clear, scalable plan. They must also be comfortable influencing senior leaders, challenging existing assumptions, and establishing new processes across multiple organizations.

Key job responsibilities
- Develop the end-to-end business plan and leadership proposal for Quick Commerce’s 3P operating model.
- Define a scalable approach for third-party partners to source, secure, launch, and operate Quick Commerce sites.
- Evaluate potential 3P models, including under-the-roof operations, site acquisition, launch support, ongoing operations, and fully outsourced solutions.
- Partner with GPO to identify, evaluate, and qualify potential third-party operators and supporting suppliers.
- Work with Finance to develop detailed financial models, cost benchmarks, investment requirements, and comparisons against first-party operations.
- Partner with Legal to define contractual frameworks, compliance requirements, liability structures, performance expectations, and appropriate controls.
- Work with Real Estate and Operations to establish site requirements, approval processes, launch standards, and operating mechanisms.
- Use internal and external benchmarks to assess partner economics, operating structures, launch timelines, and scaling potential.
- Develop clear assessments of financial, operational, customer experience, compliance, and execution risks, along with proposed mitigations.
- Define pilot requirements, success criteria, performance metrics, governance mechanisms, and the roadmap for scaling beyond the initial launch.
- Establish clear ownership and integration points across Amazon and third-party partners throughout site development, launch, and steady-state operations.
- Create mechanisms to monitor partner performance, identify gaps, and drive continuous improvement.
- Prepare and present business proposals, recommendations, and decision documents to senior leadership.
- Drive alignment and execution across teams with different priorities, constraints, and areas of ownership.

A day in the life
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners and their children. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment.

The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
- Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
- Maternity and Parental Leave Options
- Paid Time Off (PTO)
- 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you!

At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

Description of Job

The Colorado Department of Personnel & Administration, Division of Human Resources (DHR) provides decentralized human resources for the State of Colorado. DHR is responsible for the oversight and coordination of all state agency human resources functions, including compensation, benefits, recruitment and selection, the employee assistance program (CSEAP), learning and development, equity, and labor relations.

This position leads the statewide Labor Relations Unit within DPA and provides leadership, governance, and management of the labor-management relationship across the State. The position provides direction to program staff as well as human resources, management and supervisors across the State in labor relations including the negotiation, implementation, and monitoring of Partnership Agreements (collective bargaining agreements).

As the Labor Relations Director, the position is responsible for the daily operations associated with working with a diverse and dynamic user group responsible for the administration of partnership agreements (collective bargaining agreements) with agencies, Institutions of Higher Education, and the State’s certified employee organization, Colorado WINS. The position also identifies opportunities for staff development and innovation as we operationalize partnership agreements, developing effective partnerships with management/employees, union representatives and other key stakeholders to ensure effective resolution through collaboration; and providing timely, competent and relevant advice, recommendations and guidance for labor and employment matters.

A summary of the duties and responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:


Strategic Business and Unit Management:


  • Provide program leadership to deliver results including serving as a strategic business partner for the Human Resources community throughout state government, conduct ongoing needs assessments to ascertain the goals and objectives of the customers;

  • Develop annual unit goals and objectives aligned with the needs of the customers and State leadership and develop and implement use of key performance indicators for Labor Relations functions within State government.

  • Analyze existing policy and process gaps, and develop solutions to close them.

  • Ensure the daily operations of the Labor Relations Unit are consistent with DPA and DHR goals and priorities.

  • Using metrics and other methods evaluate the effectiveness of the Labor Relations Unit on a regular basis and make recommendations for changes to the unit to best align with strategic goals.

  • Responsible for managing the Labor Relations Unit, including performance management and issuing any progressive discipline.

  • Respond to grievances and disputes.

  • Prioritize assignments and projects to achieve objectives and target dates, monitor workflow and workloads.

  • Evaluate the effectiveness of labor relations training and support to identify opportunities to improve the unit's methods.

Program Management - Labor Relations:
  • Program Management: Manage and oversee all aspects of the partnership agreements (collective bargaining agreements).
  • Support the creation and on-going implementation of long-term strategic plan for the Labor Relations Unit that meets the current and future needs of the State including, but not limited to, strategy and goals for labor relations, statewide contract negotiations (partnership agreements), grievance processes, and an integrated communications plan to communicate with employees, HRDs, and other partners.
  • Serves as an expert in labor relations providing advice and consultation to internal clients, including HR and operations department/agency leaders in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
Contract Negotiations: Lead and participate in labor/management workgroups.
  • Key leader in the negotiation of the Statewide Partnership Agreement and serves as lead negotiator.
  • Provides leadership and oversight of the negotiation of state entity agreements and administration of these agreements.
Grievance Management: Working with the State Personnel Director, or their designee, leads the
  • Labor Relations Unit to hear Level II Partnership Agreement Disputes. Must apply knowledge of personnel rules, labor laws, partnership agreements, federal, state and local laws in the resolution of disputes.
  • Leads Labor Relations Unit to preserve documentation and maintain a standard filing system for all disputes.
  • Develops policies and procedures to ensure that all activities within the areas of responsibilities are in compliance with applicable law, personnel rule, and policies.
  • Review and comment on new legislation with Labor impact.
  • Draft assigned portions of budget requests and responses.
Advice and Consultation:
  • Provide information and advice to leadership and human resources professionals regarding labor issues, practices, policies, and regulations.
  • Provide leadership, advice and consultation to agency supervisors, managers, HR Directors and Labor Relations staff directing, guiding, advising staff on labor relations matters to ensure proper interpretation and administration of contract provisions and avoid misunderstandings that may lead to employee dissatisfaction, grievances and unfair labor practices.
  • Maintain knowledge of the field, other functions within DHR, and the state personnel system.
  • Partner with other Division Leaders to support and collaborate on Division’s goals and objectives.
  • Provide backup to other team members as necessary.

title: Operations Supervisor, Quick Commerce
description:
Please be aware that this role requires a commitment of 32 hours per week.

Location: Couldson

Operations is the heart and soul of everything Amazon does. It is thanks to effective operations that items are processed and dispatched to our customers on time. Being an Operations Lead/Supervisor gives you the chance to see how all the different parts of operations work and play a role in making sure everything runs smoothly.

You’ll be the first point of contact for team members during their shift and help them follow the processes that your managers have put in place. This is a hands-on role, which will give you experience in using the tools and systems that make our operations successful.

Key job responsibilities
Measure and monitor workflows, track onsite performance, and provide important shift information to frontline management to ensure operational excellence across shifts
Support and train employees to deliver great service and supervise them in their daily tasks
Support the Shift/Area Manager with projects to improve processes, cultivate a safe working environment, and increase workforce engagement
Work with other departments to find solutions to address common issues or support needs in areas of key performance
Use data analysis to identify ways to optimise safety, quality and productivity

A day in the life
As an Operations Lead/Supervisor, you’ll be based in one of our operational sites. You’ll support your Shift/Area Manager to carry out the plan for the shift. That will involve helping with pre-shift meetings with your team and monitoring procedures to make sure everyone is following safety rules, quality processes, and the priority plan for the day.

You’ll escalate any issues you spot to your manager, but sometimes you’ll be the most senior person on shift and will give people the direction they need to complete their tasks. At other times, you’ll support your Shift/Area Manager in planning shifts to make sure you have enough team members working during peak times.

About the team
Quick Commerce (QC) delivers ultra-fast convenience through our network of small warehouse in city center locations, partnering with last-mile delivery providers to get products to customers in 30 minutes or less. We combine creative thinking and technological innovation to fulfill millions of urgent shopping missions, offering a curated selection of grocery items and Amazon essentials.
Our operations have two key components. Our 'under the roof' associates process orders with industry-leading speed, picking and packing customer orders to enable our 30-minute delivery promise. We operate with a people-first approach, with teams working across morning and afternoon shifts to serve customers seven days a week.
Meanwhile, our 'on the road' delivery network primarily utilizes Amazon Flex delivery partners on e-bikes specially optimized for rapid urban delivery. We continuously innovate to improve customer experience, focusing on sustainable delivery solutions in dense urban areas while maintaining strict quality and food safety standards.
Our team combines the best of Amazon's retail and logistics expertise, leveraging both Fresh and AMZL operational excellence. We foster a collaborative environment that encourages creative problem-solving and continuous improvement, as we work to revolutionize convenience shopping through ultra-fast delivery.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, AI-native
description:
About the role

  • We’re hiring into the AI team. You’ll design and build the agentic layer of the product: the loop itself, the tools agents call, how context is selected and served, and the evaluation that proves it works. Not a chat feature. The engine.

What you'll do

  • Agents that operate on governed enterprise data models, with a human in the loop.
  • Serving the right context to an agent for a given task, out of models with thousands of objects.
  • MCP tools that let external agents work with the platform safely: permissions, attribution, audit.
  • Evaluation infrastructure that tells us, measurably, whether any of it is working.
  • What AI-native means here: Your first move is an agent, not autocomplete. You’ve shipped AI into products: MCP servers or clients, agent architectures, tool-use frameworks, context pipelines, LLM integrations in production. You think about control flow, tool interfaces, memory, and how to know when the loop is wrong. We’re not hiring an API caller.

Qualifications

  • Proficiency in English
  • Stack: Strongly typed languages.
    • We run C#, Rust and TypeScript, and the list is a proxy for thinking in systems and types rather than a requirement to know all three.
    • Deep fluency in any of C#, Rust, Go, Java or TypeScript and willingness to work across them.
    • AWS, APIs, production systems.
  • Walk us through an agentic system you built and shipped, production or serious open source. What the loop did, where it broke, how you evaluated it. If you can’t, this isn’t the role, regardless of seniority.

How we work

  • Small senior team, high ownership, fast releases. Eighteen features shipped in August. The team is distributed across the US, Europe and South America, and you’ll work in overlapping hours with US Pacific. Your work lands in a new revenue line within the quarter.
  • This role is employed through a local employer of record in your country of residence. Your employment contract, payroll, benefits, and statutory contributions are administered locally in full compliance with local labor law. Your day-to-day work is with the SqlDBM team.


What we offer

  • Competitive base salary and equity in a profitable, growing company
  • Fully remote
  • Direct impact on product direction — small team, no layers, your work ships to enterprise customers
  • Work on genuinely hard technical problems at the frontier of AI and enterprise data infrastructure
  • Collaborative, engineering-driven culture that moves fast and trusts its people
  • Paid vacation at or above the statutory entitlement in your country of residence, which varies by country and length of service.
  • All public holidays observed in your country of residence, in addition to paid vacation.
  • Statutory 13th-month pay, paid on the schedule set by local law.
  • Paid sick leave and parental leave in line with local statutory entitlements.
  • Employer-funded social security and mandatory local benefits, administered locally.

title: Petroleum Scientist 1, 2, or 3 (Enforcement)
description:
About this Job

Office of Enforcement – Orders-State

The Office of Enforcement (OENF) is dedicated to ensuring regulatory compliance and protecting public and environmental interests through rigorous inspection programs, timely enforcement actions and transparent oversight. The Office emphasizes proactive monitoring, consistent regulatory enforcement and transparent reporting. Its operations are designed to uphold compliance standards, swiftly address violations and maintain trust and accountability within Louisiana’s regulated community.

The Petroleum Scientist 1, 2, or 3 reviews Lease Facility Inspections, Drilling and Workover inspections, Production Pit Inspections, Reserve Pit Inspections, and Narrative Reports submitted by Office of Enforcement Conservation Enforcement Specialists to ensure compliance with the rules and regulations of the Office of Enforcement, and when appropriate, writes Compliance Orders-and where applicable, recommends Civil Penalties or further regulatory actions regarding deficiencies for oil and gas production facilities and oilfield pits.


Minimum Qualifications

A bachelor’s degree in a geoscience field or engineering.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

This position is located in the Baton Rouge Office with a core function of monitoring compliance with rules and regulations of oil and gas operators within the State of Louisiana. Additional duties include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Reviews Lease Facility Inspections, Drilling and Workover inspections, Production Pit Inspections, Reserve Pit Inspections, and Narrative Reports submitted by Office of Enforcement Conservation Enforcement Specialists to ensure compliance with the rules and regulations of the Office of Enforcement and when appropriate writes Compliance Orders and where applicable recommends Civil Penalties or further regulatory actions regarding deficiencies for oil and gas production facilities and oilfield pits. It is the responsibility of the incumbent to ensure that violations are corrected in a timely manner.
  • Responsible for handling complaints from land owners or concerned citizens regarding oil and gas operation in the vicinity of the their property. This includes contacting the appropriate District Manager for the dispatch of a CES to investigate and inspect the area in question. Further, if any violations are noted, it is the incumbent’s duty to initiate corrective action and keep complainant informed of all actions taken by this Office.
  • Reviews information requests generated by other sections—such as Production Audit, Well Files, NRTA, and Permitting—and, when appropriate, prepares and issues Compliance Orders requiring the regulated party to provide the requested information or make required payments and where applicable recommends Civil Penalties or further regulatory actions regarding deficiencies for these departments.
  • Reviews unit survey plats submitted for units created by field orders issued by the Executive Director of Enforcement and either approves of rejects same.
  • Responsible for processing site clearance applications and reviewing site clearance verification reports to ensure compliance with all applicable rules and regulations.
  • Responsible for gathering information and conducting inspections related to all Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) hearings resulting from their 10-day letters.
  • May accompany CES on field inspections to ensure compliance with rules and regulations of the Office of Enforcement via helicopter, seaplane, boat, and/or vehicle, as applicable.

Position-Specific Details:

Appointment Type: This vacancy is being announced as a classified position and is open to all qualified applicants. This position may be filled as a fulltime Classified Probationary appointment or as a Job Appointment (a temporary appointment up to 4 years).

In the event that funds become available for a permanent position, the employee may be converted to a probational appointment. Additional Vacancies may be filled from this announcement within 90 days of the closing date

Career Progression: This position participates in a Career Progression Group up to the Petroleum Scientist 3.

Work Schedule: Work hours are flexible.

Compensation: The salary offered will be determined based on qualifications and experience.

title: IT Director
description:
Lead the strategy. Support the people. Own the results.

Branson Bank is looking for an IT Director who can guide technology strategy, strengthen cybersecurity, and lead daily IT operations while remaining ready to help an employee troubleshoot a problem.

This is a visible, onsite leadership role for someone who enjoys building relationships, developing others, and taking ownership from the first conversation through resolution. You will work closely with bank leadership, internal IT personnel, and technology partners to keep the bank’s systems secure, reliable, and aligned with its business goals.

Whether you are developing a technology roadmap, preparing for an audit, holding a vendor accountable, or providing support while a teammate is out, your contribution will directly support the people who keep the bank running.

What You Will Do

  • Lead technology strategy and operations. Develop practical technology roadmaps, guide infrastructure and system improvements, and help leadership make informed decisions about technology investments, budgets, and priorities.
  • Stay involved in daily support. Maintain the technical skills and willingness to troubleshoot issues, provide coverage, and help resolve problems at their source.
  • Strengthen cybersecurity and risk management. Oversee security practices, policies, vulnerability management, access controls, and incident preparedness. Serve as, or grow into serving as, the bank’s Information Security Officer.
  • Support banking compliance. Coordinate technology and security responsibilities related to regulatory examinations, audits, risk assessments, business continuity, and disaster recovery. Track findings through resolution.
  • Manage vendors with a trust-but-verify approach. Evaluate recommendations, monitor service quality, review contracts and risks, and ensure providers deliver on their commitments. Maintain internal accountability for outcomes.
  • Deliver technology projects. Lead initiatives from planning and scope development through implementation, employee adoption, documentation, and follow-up.
  • Champion responsible AI and automation. Guide the evaluation, governance, implementation, and ongoing oversight of tools that improve efficiency while protecting bank and customer information.
  • Develop the IT team. Set clear expectations, assign priorities, mentor employees, coordinate coverage, and support professional growth.
  • Communicate clearly. Translate technical issues, risks, and recommendations into practical information for employees, executive leadership, and the Board.
  • Contribute to the bank’s culture. Be approachable, treat others with respect, celebrate accomplishments, and step in wherever your help can make a difference.

What You Bring

  • Significant professional experience supporting IT environments, with a strong foundation in infrastructure, systems administration, networking, cybersecurity, and end-user support.
  • Demonstrated experience leading technology initiatives, projects, vendors, or employees.
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and carry projects from planning through completion.
  • An understanding of information security, technology risk, and banking technology expectations, including FFIEC guidance, GLBA, vendor oversight, business continuity, and disaster recovery.
  • Strong troubleshooting, organizational, and communication skills.
  • The ability to connect technology decisions to business needs, costs, risks, and results.
  • A collaborative leadership style and a willingness to personally assist with day-to-day needs.
  • The ability and willingness to work onsite and build regular working relationships with employees and leadership.

Experience That Will Help You Stand Out

  • Banking, credit union, or other financial institution technology experience.
  • Seven or more years of progressively responsible IT experience, including leadership responsibilities.
  • A bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, cybersecurity, business, or a related field.
  • Experience serving as an Information Security Officer or supporting a financial institution’s Information Security Program.
  • Experience with banking audits, regulatory examinations, IT risk assessments, and vendor management.
  • Familiarity with CSI NuPoint or similar banking technology and core service providers.
  • Experience developing strategic plans, technology budgets, roadmaps, and Board-level reporting.
  • Experience implementing or governing AI and automation.
  • Relevant technology, cybersecurity, banking, or project management certifications.

How You Lead Matters

Branson Bank is seeking someone who follows through, communicates openly, and remains calm when situations become challenging. You should enjoy mentoring others, sharing knowledge, and helping colleagues succeed.

An ownership mindset is essential. When something needs attention, you help move it toward resolution. You treat employees, customers, and partners with the same professionalism and respect you would expect in return, and you take time to recognize individual and team accomplishments.

Work Schedule and Expectations

This is a full-time, onsite position with a typical schedule of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional evening or weekend work may be necessary to support bank operations.

Interested in Joining Branson Bank?

If you enjoy combining technology leadership with practical problem-solving and service to others, we encourage you to apply.

Team / division overview

DWS’s data infrastructure team provides the secure, scalable and trustworthy foundation for storing, processing and distributing critical enterprise data. As Lead Engineer - Data Platform, you drive the design, built, and continuous improvement of our hybrid data platform. You’ll lead a small but high-impact team, setting technical direction, mentoring team members and contributing directly to architecture and code.


Your responsibilities –

As our Lead Engineer – Data Platform, you will:



  • Own the end-to-end architecture, design and evolution of enterprise data platform capabilities across hybrid cloud and on-premises environments
  • Define the technical roadmap, engineering standards and reusable patterns for workflow orchestration, scheduling, dependency management and data processing
  • Lead architectural decisions, proofs of concept and adoption plans based on scalability, interoperability, security, operability and total cost of ownership
  • Establish reliability, observability and operational standards for data platform components, including monitoring, alerting, failure recovery, capacity management and service-level objectives
  • Drive platform automation through infrastructure as code, CI/CD, automated testing and self-service engineering capabilities
  • Partner with architecture, security, governance and application teams to ensure platform solutions meet enterprise standards and regulatory requirements
  • Remain hands-on in architecture and code, lead design and code reviews, mentor engineers and foster a culture of engineering excellence and continuous improvement

We are looking for



  • 12+ years of experience in data or platform engineering, including designing and operating enterprise-scale data platforms; a relevant degree is advantageous
  • Deep hands-on Snowflake expertise across architecture, ingestion, transformation, workload management, performance, cost optimisation, secure data sharing and governance
  • Strong production experience with Apache Airflow, including reusable DAG patterns, dependency management, scheduling, testing, monitoring and failure recovery
  • Strong expertise in Apache Kafka and event-driven architectures, including topic design, producers and consumers, schema management, Kafka Connect, delivery semantics and replay strategies
  • Proven ability to integrate batch and streaming pipelines across Snowflake, Airflow and Kafka
  • Advanced Python and SQL skills; Java experience for Kafka-based services and connectors is beneficial
  • Strong experience with Terraform, Git, CI/CD and automated testing; OpenShift or Kubernetes experience is desirable
  • Strong understanding of reliability, observability, data quality, security, access management and compliance in regulated environments
  • Proven technical leadership, including setting engineering direction, reviewing designs and code, mentoring engineers and communicating with technical and business stakeholders
  • Strong problem-solving and strategic-thinking skills, with fluent written and spoken English
  • Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimise workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs

What we’ll offer you:

At DWS we’re serious about diversity, equity and creating an inclusive culture where colleagues can be themselves sand it’s important to us that you enjoy coming to work - feeling healthy, happy and rewarded. At DWS, you’ll have access to a range of benefits which you can choose from to create a personalised plan unique to your lifestyle. Whether you’re interested in healthcare, company perks, or are thinking about your retirement plan, there’s something for everyone.


DWS’ Hybrid Working model is designed to find the right balance between in-person collaboration and engagement in the office, which is core to our working culture, and working from home. Each business group varies on the split between time spent in the office and at home, but this will be discussed and made clear as part of your application and interview process. We will continue to review and evolve our working environments and methods to ensure that we are working in the best way possible for our people.


If you require any adjustments or changes to be made to the interview process for any reason including, or related to a disability or long‑term health condition, then please contact your recruiter and let them know what assistance you may need. Examples of adjustments include providing a change to the format of the interview, or providing assistance when at the DWS office. This will not affect your application and your recruitment team will discuss options with you

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assist licensed electricians and journeyman electricians with the installation, assembly, modification, and repair of electrical systems, including conduit, wiring, panels, switchgear, and electrical components used in commercial applications
  • Support routine maintenance and repair of electrical equipment, fixtures, motors, and control devices under supervision
  • Assist with troubleshooting electrical system issues, including power failures, control malfunctions, and equipment connectivity problems
  • Learn to interpret and work from blueprints, electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical drawings
  • Measure, cut, bend, thread, and install conduit and pull wire as directed
  • Assist with testing and verification of electrical systems using appropriate meters and diagnostic tools under supervision
  • Prepare, organize, and maintain tools, materials, parts, and equipment needed for assigned work
  • Communicate work progress, questions, and jobsite needs to supervisors, electricians, technicians, and project team members
  • Complete assigned tasks in a professional manner that meets customer and company standards
  • Maintain accurate notes and documentation as directed, including work performed, materials used, test results, and photos
  • Comply with all company policies, jobsite procedures, and applicable electrical and safety codes
  • Maintain a clean, organized work area and properly care for assigned tools and equipment
  • Travel to various job sites as required
  • Perform other related duties within the scope of an electrical apprenticeship as assigned

Required Skills and Qualifications

  • Interest in building a career in the electrical trade and willingness to learn through hands-on training
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to use hand tools and power tools safely
  • Ability to follow directions, established procedures, and detailed work instructions
  • Ability to read and interpret basic technical information, with a willingness to develop blueprint and electrical drawing skills
  • Strong communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and time management skills
  • Dependable, safety-focused, and able to maintain productivity and quality standards under supervision
  • Prior experience with commercial, industrial, construction, maintenance, or trade work preferred but not required

Certifications and Education

  • High school diploma or GED preferred
  • Enrollment in or willingness to enroll in an electrical apprenticeship program or related trade training preferred
  • OSHA safety training preferred
  • Valid state driver’s license required and must be maintained
  • Additional electrical, construction, or safety training preferred

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions

  • Regularly required to stand, walk, climb, bend, kneel, reach, push, and pull
  • Must be able to lift, carry, and handle materials weighing up to 75 pounds
  • Work is performed in commercial and industrial environments, including indoor and outdoor settings
  • Exposure to moderate noise levels, energized equipment, and varying temperatures

Additional Information

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (Node/React) - Remote
description:
Senior Full Stack Engineer (Node/React) - Remote

Kake is a remote-first company and a people-first global community of senior engineers. Kake engineers are behind some of the world’s most innovative products (Brands you’ve heard!), from Fortune 500 to fast-growing companies. We believe it’s not where your table is, but what you bring to the table that matters. Our community spans 45,000+ engineers across 55+ countries; join a culture where great people stay, grow, and thrive (and love eating kake!).

We’re looking for Senior Software Engineers specializing in Node.js/React, skilled in building high-performance, scalable systems that support millions of users, and committed to solid architectural judgment and engineering best practices. It's a great fit for people who enjoy owning problems end-to-end, working across the stack, and collaborating closely with product and design to ship reliable, well-crafted software.

What you’ll build and own

  • Build and ship production features end-to-end across Node.js backends and React frontends, owning your work from implementation through deployment.
  • Design, build, and version REST or GraphQL APIs that serve as the contract between frontend and backend systems.
  • Make architecture decisions around data modelling, service boundaries, and component design, applying event-driven thinking where it fits.
  • Model and query data across relational and NoSQL stores, choosing the right database and structure for each use case.
  • Write clean, well-tested code and set up the observability needed to catch and debug issues in live systems.

Core Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in software engineering, with hands-on work in Node.js and React.
  • Hands-on experience designing and versioning REST or GraphQL APIs.
  • Experience with modern git workflows, CI/CD, and cloud infrastructure such as GCP, AWS, or Azure.
  • Strong system-design instincts: data modelling, component architecture, and event-driven thinking.
  • Comfortable with relational databases and SQL, plus familiarity with NoSQL such as MongoDB or similar.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills across distributed systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote, fast-paced environment.

Nice-to-Have

  • AI-forward mindset with active use of AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to accelerate delivery, while staying the engineer who judges correctness.
  • Experience with e-commerce, payments, video platforms, or other correctness-critical domains is a strong plus.
  • Availability to work aligned with the partner's time zone.

Additional

  • US Timezone Overlap: 6h-7h daily PST

Why Join Kake?

  • Competitive Pay in USD: Work globally, get paid globally.
  • Fully Remote: Simply put, we trust you.
  • Better Me Fund: We invest in your personal growth and passions.
  • Compassion is Badass: Join a community that invests in social good.

Company Overview
